area: Claude Code native support for CLAUDE.md, memory, rule files, path scoping, imports, /doctor, /init, managed CLAUDE.md, and auto-memory, as of 2026-09-28 (docs at code.claude.com/docs/en/memory and code.claude.com/docs/en/common-workflows)

facts.behavior: "CLAUDE.md files are markdown files that give Claude persistent instructions for a project, your personal workflow, or your entire organization. You write these files in plain text; Claude reads them at the start of every session."
facts.limits: Recommended target: under 200 lines per file (longer files 'consume more context and reduce adherence'). Hard cap: Claude Code loads a CLAUDE.md of up to 4 MiB in full and skips (does not load) a larger file.

facts.feature: CLAUDE.md vs auto memory — not enforced configuration
facts.behavior: "Claude treats them as context, not enforced configuration. To block an action regardless of what Claude decides, use a PreToolUse hook instead." "CLAUDE.md content is delivered as a user message after the system prompt, not as part of the system prompt itself. Claude reads it and tries to follow it, but there's no guarantee of strict compliance, especially for vague or conflicting instructions."
facts.limits: Applies to every scope of CLAUDE.md including the managed/org one: "Settings rules are enforced by the client regardless of what Claude decides to do. CLAUDE.md instructions shape Claude's behavior but are not a hard enforcement layer." For real enforcement, docs point to PreToolUse hooks or managed settings (permissions.deny, sandbox.enabled, env).

facts.behavior: Deployed at a fixed OS path (macOS /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/CLAUDE.md; Linux/WSL /etc/claude-code/CLAUDE.md; Windows C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\CLAUDE.md) via MDM/Group Policy/Ansible. "This file cannot be excluded by individual settings." Precedence: "Loads before user and project CLAUDE.md." Alternatively, the `claudeMd` key in managed-settings.json can hold the content directly instead of a separate file.
facts.limits: Scope: every session on the machine, in every repository. Only honored via managed/policy settings — "Setting claudeMd in user, project, or local settings has no effect." claudeMdExcludes cannot remove it.

facts.feature: User, project, and local CLAUDE.md scopes
facts.behavior: Four scopes load in this order (broadest to most specific): managed policy, `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (user), `./CLAUDE.md` or `./.claude/CLAUDE.md` (project, team-shared via source control), and `./CLAUDE.local.md` (personal, meant to be gitignored).
facts.limits: "CLAUDE.md and CLAUDE.local.md files in the directory hierarchy above the working directory are loaded at launch. Files in subdirectories load on demand when Claude reads files in those directories."

facts.feature: CLAUDE.md concatenation and ordering, not override
facts.behavior: "All discovered files are concatenated into context rather than overriding each other. Across the directory tree, content is ordered from the filesystem root down to your working directory... Within each directory, CLAUDE.local.md is appended after CLAUDE.md, so your personal notes are the last thing Claude reads at that level."
facts.limits: Because files are concatenated rather than merged/deduped, conflicting instructions across files are possible: "if two rules contradict each other, Claude may pick one arbitrarily."

facts.behavior: "Claude also discovers CLAUDE.md and CLAUDE.local.md files in subdirectories under your current working directory. Instead of loading them at launch, they are included when Claude reads files in those subdirectories." Also: "@ file references add CLAUDE.md in the file's directory and parent directories to context."
facts.limits: Only triggers on Claude reading a file in that subdirectory — not loaded proactively at session start.

facts.behavior: "Block-level HTML comments (<!-- maintainer notes -->) in CLAUDE.md files are stripped before the content is injected into Claude's context. Use them to leave notes for human maintainers without spending context tokens on them."
facts.limits: Comments inside code blocks are preserved (not stripped). Reading the file directly with the Read tool still shows comments.

facts.behavior: "By default, CLAUDE.md files from these [--add-dir] directories are not loaded." Setting CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD=1 loads "CLAUDE.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules/*.md, and CLAUDE.local.md from the additional directory."
facts.limits: CLAUDE.local.md from the additional directory is skipped if `local` is excluded from --setting-sources.

facts.behavior: "CLAUDE.md files can import additional files using @path/to/import syntax. Imported files are expanded and loaded into context at launch alongside the CLAUDE.md that references them." Both relative and absolute paths allowed; relative paths resolve relative to the file containing the import, not the working directory.
facts.limits: "Imported files can recursively import other files, with a maximum depth of four hops." Splitting into imports "helps organization but doesn't reduce context, since imported files load at launch."

facts.behavior: "Import parsing skips Markdown code spans and fenced code blocks. To mention a path in your CLAUDE.md without importing it, wrap it in backticks: writing `@README` (in backticks) keeps the text literal, while @README outside backticks imports the file."
facts.limits: Only applies to backtick code spans/fenced blocks; plain-text mentions of an @path elsewhere are treated as imports.

facts.behavior: "An import in a project-level memory file is external when its path resolves outside your working directory... The first time Claude Code encounters external imports in a project, it shows an approval dialog listing the files. If you decline, the imports stay disabled and the dialog doesn't appear again." User-scope memory files (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, ~/.claude/rules/) load their imports without this dialog (except in Cowork desktop sessions).
facts.limits: Applies only to project-level (not user-level) memory files; in Cowork desktop sessions, imports resolving outside the working directory in a user-scope file are skipped rather than prompted, and symlinked/hardlinked ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md or rule files pointing outside the working directory are also skipped.

facts.behavior: "For larger projects, you can organize instructions into multiple files using the .claude/rules/ directory... All .md files are discovered recursively, so you can organize rules into subdirectories." "Rules without paths frontmatter are loaded at launch with the same priority as .claude/CLAUDE.md."
facts.limits: "Project rules are skipped if you exclude project from --setting-sources. Before v2.1.211, rules that load on demand, including path-scoped rules and rules in nested .claude/rules/ directories, loaded even when project was excluded."

facts.behavior: Rules can be scoped via YAML frontmatter `paths:` field with glob patterns; "These conditional rules only apply when Claude is working with files matching the specified patterns." "Path-scoped rules trigger when Claude reads files matching the pattern, not on every tool use." Supports brace expansion, e.g. `src/**/*.{ts,tsx}`.
facts.limits: "Rules without a paths field are loaded unconditionally and apply to all files." As of v2.1.198, matching also works through a symlinked path to the project directory.

facts.behavior: "Each brace group multiplies the number of expanded patterns... To keep expansion bounded, a rule's whole paths list shares one budget of 1,000 expanded patterns and 4 MiB, and patterns without braces don't count against it. Claude Code uses any pattern that would exceed the budget unexpanded, and its literal braces match no files."
facts.limits: 1,000 expanded patterns / 4 MiB per rule's paths list. Before v2.1.217, an over-budget paths value "stalled or crashed the CLI at startup" (now degrades gracefully instead).

facts.feature: Invalid glob bracket handling in paths
facts.behavior: "A pattern with a [ that can't be read as a bracket expression, such as photos [2024/**, is invalid: it matches nothing, and the rule's other patterns keep working." Escape a literal `[` as `\[`.
facts.limits: Before v2.1.207, one invalid pattern made the Read tool fail for every file the rule was evaluated against, instead of just matching nothing.

facts.behavior: "paths is the only field Claude Code reads from a rule; any other field is ignored without an error. Claude Code removes the frontmatter before loading the rule into context." "If the YAML between the markers doesn't parse, Claude Code ignores the frontmatter and loads the rule as if it had no paths. Run claude --debug to see the parse error."
facts.limits: paths accepts a YAML list or comma-separated string; no other frontmatter fields have any effect.

facts.behavior: ".claude/rules/ directory supports symlinks, so you can maintain a shared set of rules and link them into multiple projects. Circular symlinks are detected and handled gracefully." A symlink whose target is outside the working directory is treated like an external import: "The linked rules don't load until you approve external imports for the project, and after that only the ones without a paths field load."
facts.limits: External-import approval is triggered only by an @path import in a project memory file, not by symlinks alone. Network paths (UNC shares, /net, /Network) in a rules or CLAUDE.md symlink target never load — "Claude Code doesn't follow the link, because looking up such a path can contact the host it names" (\\wsl$ is exempt).

facts.behavior: "Personal rules in ~/.claude/rules/ apply to every project on your machine." "Claude Code loads user-level rules before project rules, so a project rule appears later in Claude's context than a user rule. Neither set overrides the other: if a user rule and a project rule conflict, Claude may follow either one, so keep the two consistent."
facts.limits: No override semantics; conflicts are unresolved by the harness (advisory only), and this is also the documented way to load shared rules without triggering the external-import approval dialog.

facts.behavior: "The claudeMdExcludes setting lets you skip specific files by path or glob pattern." "Patterns are matched against absolute file paths using glob syntax." Configurable at user, project, local, or managed policy settings layer; "Arrays merge across layers."
facts.limits: "Managed policy CLAUDE.md files cannot be excluded." For a symlinked rule, before v2.1.239 only a pattern matching the link target excluded the file (now either the .claude/rules/ path or the link target works).

facts.behavior: "Claude Code can read AGENTS.md as your project instructions, so a repository already set up for other coding agents works without adding a CLAUDE.md, an import, or a setting." Default: Claude reads AGENTS.md "only when you have no CLAUDE.md or CLAUDE.local.md in your working directory or above it"; otherwise CLAUDE.md wins. AGENTS.local.md, AGENTS.override.md, and anything under .agents/ are never read.
facts.limits: Requires Claude Code v2.1.277+ (and v2.1.281+ for some session types e.g. Bedrock/telemetry-disabled). Reading AGENTS.md directly does not fire InstructionsLoaded hooks (those fire only for CLAUDE.md, or for an AGENTS.md reached via a CLAUDE.md import/symlink); AGENTS.md doesn't load from --add-dir directories even with CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD set; external-import approval doesn't prompt for AGENTS.md (loads only if already approved).

facts.behavior: Four values control which instruction files load: `claude-md-or-agents-md` (default: CLAUDE.md, or AGENTS.md only if no CLAUDE.md/CLAUDE.local.md exists), `claude-md-and-agents-md` (both, CLAUDE.md first), `claude-md` (CLAUDE.md only), `managed-only` ("Only your organization's managed CLAUDE.md and auto memory at launch. Your project, local, and user CLAUDE.md files, your .claude/rules/ files, and every AGENTS.md are left out." though subdirectory CLAUDE.md/rules and path-scoped rules still load on demand).
facts.limits: Also settable via pluginConfigs["agents-md@builtin"].options.instructionFiles in user/--settings/managed settings; "Claude Code ignores it in project and local settings files." Change applies from the next message/new session.

facts.behavior: "Run /init to generate a starting CLAUDE.md automatically. Claude analyzes your codebase and creates a file with build commands, test instructions, and project conventions it discovers. If a CLAUDE.md already exists, /init suggests improvements rather than overwriting it." It also migrates from other tools' rule files: Cursor rules (.cursor/rules/, .cursorrules), Copilot rules (.github/copilot-instructions.md).
facts.limits: With CLAUDE_CODE_NEW_INIT=1 set, migration also covers AGENTS.md, .devin/rules/, .windsurf/rules/ or .windsurfrules, and .clinerules, and /init becomes an interactive multi-phase flow (asks which artifacts to set up — CLAUDE.md, skills, hooks — explores via subagent, asks follow-ups, presents a reviewable proposal before writing).

facts.behavior: "You can also run /import to bring a supported coding agent's configuration into Claude Code, which appends a one-time copy of instruction files such as AGENTS.md to the matching CLAUDE.md and carries over MCP servers, commands, subagents, and skills."
facts.limits: Requires Claude Code v2.1.213 or later.

facts.behavior: "Claude reads your CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, and AGENTS.md files, plus the rules, skills, commands, subagents, and output styles under .claude/ and ~/.claude/. It looks for problems such as instructions written for older models, references to files or commands that don't exist, and files that contradict each other. You get a report of findings and a set of proposed edits, and nothing in your files changes until you ask Claude to apply them." Can be scoped to one file/dir: `/doctor prompt-audit .claude/skills/deploy`.
facts.limits: Runs through the bundled /claude-api skill, so it's unavailable if that skill is turned off via skillOverrides or disableBundledSkills. Requires Claude Code v2.1.283 or later.

facts.behavior: "The /doctor checkup proposes trims for a checked-in CLAUDE.md: it cuts content Claude can derive from the codebase, such as directory layouts, dependency lists, and architecture overviews, and keeps pitfalls, rationale, and conventions that differ from tool defaults."
facts.limits: Requires Claude Code v2.1.206 or later.

facts.behavior: "If one of your instruction files is over the recommended length, you see a warning at startup and when you run /status. You also see a warning when files that are each within that length add up past a combined limit at session start. Each CLAUDE.md, rules file, and @path import counts as a separate file."
facts.limits: Recommended per-file length is 200 lines (same threshold as the general CLAUDE.md size guidance); combined-limit trigger is separate from the per-file one.

facts.behavior: "The /memory command lists your CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, and other memory file locations across user and project scopes, including user and project CLAUDE.md entries for files that don't exist yet. It also lets you toggle auto memory on or off and provides an option to open the auto memory folder. Select any file to open it in your editor; selecting one that doesn't exist yet creates it first."
facts.limits: GUI editors open the file in a separate window without blocking the session (as of v2.1.216+); terminal editors take over the terminal until you exit.

facts.behavior: "To check which CLAUDE.md and rules files loaded into the current session, run /context." Used to confirm a project CLAUDE.md, a symlinked/imported AGENTS.md, etc. actually loaded (listed under 'Memory files').
facts.limits: Before v2.1.280, /memory and /context didn't list an AGENTS.md that Claude read directly.

facts.behavior: "Auto memory lets Claude accumulate knowledge across sessions without you writing anything. As it works, Claude saves four kinds of notes for itself": `user` (role/expertise/preferences), `feedback` (corrections and confirmed approaches), `project` (ongoing work, deadlines, decisions not derivable from code/git history), `reference` (where to find outside information). "Claude skips anything it can derive from the codebase... It also skips anything your CLAUDE.md files already say." "Claude doesn't save something every session. It decides what's worth remembering."
facts.limits: Judgment-based — no guarantee any given fact is saved; is on by default.

facts.behavior: "Auto memory is on by default. To toggle it, open /memory in a session and use the auto memory toggle, which saves autoMemoryEnabled to your user settings at ~/.claude/settings.json." Per-project: set `autoMemoryEnabled: false` in that project's settings. Env var: `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1`.
facts.limits: Three independent ways to disable (UI toggle/user settings, project settings, env var); no partial/scoped disabling (e.g., per rule-type) is documented.

facts.behavior: "Each project gets its own memory directory at ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/. The <project> path is derived from the git repository, so all worktrees and subdirectories within the same repo share one auto memory directory. Outside a git repo, the project root is used instead."
facts.limits: "Auto memory is machine-local... Files are not shared across machines or cloud environments." CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME (v2.1.234+) can force a custom shared <project> name; autoMemoryDirectory setting can relocate it, honored under the same workspace-trust rule as hooks, and is skipped entirely when permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories is on and a repo-supplied settings file points outside the working directory.

facts.behavior: "The first 200 lines of MEMORY.md, or the first 25KB, whichever comes first, are loaded at the start of every conversation. Content beyond that threshold is not loaded at session start." "After Claude writes to MEMORY.md, Claude Code measures the file against the 200-line and 25KB read limits. If the file is near a limit, Claude Code reminds Claude to shorten it... If the file is over a limit, the write still succeeds, but Claude Code returns an error telling Claude to rewrite the index, because everything past the limit is dropped on the next load."
facts.limits: Limit applies only to MEMORY.md, not to per-topic memory files, which "Claude Code doesn't load... at startup" but reads on demand. Distinct from the 4 MiB CLAUDE.md cap.

facts.behavior: "The main conversation's auto memory isn't loaded into subagents; the exception is a fork, which inherits the parent conversation and system prompt. A subagent's own auto memory, enabled with the subagent memory field, is a separate directory."
facts.limits: Only forked subagents inherit parent auto memory; ordinary subagents get none unless separately configured.

facts.behavior: "When Claude writes a memory file that begins with YAML frontmatter, Claude Code records the write time in a modified frontmatter field as an ISO 8601 timestamp... Any file that has frontmatter gets the field the next time Claude writes it, including files created on earlier versions; Claude Code never adds frontmatter to a file that has none."
facts.limits: Requires Claude Code v2.1.214 or later; only applies to files that already have (or gain) YAML frontmatter.

facts.feature: Memory files excluded from transcript cleanup
facts.behavior: "Claude Code deletes old session transcripts after the cleanupPeriodDays retention period, but excludes the memory files in the memory directory from that retention sweep. MEMORY.md and topic files stay until you or Claude edits or deletes them."
facts.limits: Applies only to the auto-memory directory, not to session transcripts generally.

facts.behavior: "Project-root CLAUDE.md survives compaction: after /compact, Claude re-reads it from disk and re-injects it into the session. Nested CLAUDE.md files in subdirectories and rules with paths: frontmatter reload as Claude reads files they apply to." "If an instruction disappeared after compaction, it was given only in conversation, lives in a nested CLAUDE.md that hasn't reloaded yet, or is a path-scoped rule that hasn't matched a file since."
facts.limits: Only project-root CLAUDE.md is guaranteed to reload automatically post-compaction; nested/path-scoped content depends on subsequent file reads matching.

facts.behavior: Sharing one instruction file via `ln -s AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md`: "Claude reads CLAUDE.md through the link, but the Edit and Write tools refuse to write through a symlink, and the refusal directs Claude to edit the link's target, AGENTS.md, instead."
facts.limits: Applies to symlinked CLAUDE.md specifically; on Windows, a committed symlink checks out as a plain-text file unless core.symlinks is enabled, so the @AGENTS.md import approach is recommended there instead.

area: Claude Code plugins as of 2026-09-28 — plugin definition/manifest, every plugin component type, marketplaces and plugin sources, `claude plugin validate`, `claude plugin details` and token-cost accounting, and whether a plugin can ship rules/CLAUDE.md context.

facts.behavior: "A Claude Code plugin is a directory of skills, agents, hooks, MCP servers, or other components that Claude Code installs and loads as one unit." A plugin is "a directory of components, usually with a manifest."
facts.limits: Applies to Claude Code (terminal, VS Code, desktop app); claude.ai and Cowork load a different subset of component types from the same plugin format.

facts.behavior: "The manifest is optional. Without it, Claude Code loads the components it finds in the standard layout. The plugin name then comes from the marketplace entry, or from the directory name when you load the plugin with --plugin-dir." name is the only required field when a manifest exists.
facts.limits: A manifest is needed only for metadata, a component outside its default directory, userConfig, or an inline component definition.

facts.feature: CLAUDE.md at the plugin root is NOT loaded as context (rules must be shipped as a skill)
facts.behavior: "A CLAUDE.md at the plugin root isn't loaded as context, and claude plugin validate warns when it finds one. To include instructions that load into Claude's context, put them in a skill." Restated on the components page: "To include instructions in a plugin, write them as a skill. Claude Code doesn't load a CLAUDE.md at the plugin root, and claude plugin validate warns `CLAUDE.md at the plugin root is not loaded as project context`."
facts.limits: Scoped specifically to a CLAUDE.md file placed at the plugin's own root directory; the plugin's other components (e.g. a skill's SKILL.md) still load normally. The file is silently excluded from context, not rejected — the plugin still loads, just without that file's content.

facts.behavior: A skill is a SKILL.md file Claude loads when its description matches the task, saved under skills/<name>/SKILL.md; the user can also run it directly as /<plugin>:<name>.
facts.limits: The skills manifest key ADDS to the default skills/ directory scan (unlike commands/agents, which it replaces). A single SKILL.md at the plugin root with no skills/ dir and no skills key loads as one skill, but without a frontmatter name it's named after the install cache directory rather than the plugin.

facts.behavior: A command is a single Markdown file the user runs by name, e.g. /<plugin>:<file>. "Commands are the older format... write new ones as skills and keep commands/ for files you already have."
facts.limits: The commands manifest key REPLACES the default commands/ scan. Each entry in the object-map form must set exactly one of source or content; an entry that sets both or neither fails validation.

facts.behavior: Each Markdown file under agents/ defines a subagent, namespaced <plugin>:<name>, invocable by Claude or explicitly by the user as @agent-<plugin>:<name>.
facts.limits: Only these frontmatter fields are supported: name, description, model, effort, maxTurns, tools, disallowedTools, skills, memory, background, omitClaudeMd, isolation (only "worktree" is valid), color, and experimental.cacheTtl. permissionMode, hooks, mcpServers, and initialPrompt are ignored — "an agent file can't add hooks or MCP servers on its own." Unparseable frontmatter still loads the agent, but named after the file with description "Agent from <plugin> plugin."

facts.behavior: Hooks run automatically at Claude Code lifecycle events (shell command, HTTP request, MCP tool call, model prompt, or subagent), declared in hooks/hooks.json and merged with the hooks manifest key.
facts.limits: "A plugin's hooks don't wait for one of the plugin's skills or commands to be used... they fire on their events from then on" for the whole session the plugin is enabled in. Matching the plugin's own MCP tools in a hook matcher requires the full name mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__<tool>; a matcher on the server name alone never fires.

facts.behavior: Declared in .mcp.json at the plugin root or the mcpServers manifest key; gives Claude tools from an external system. Server appears as plugin:<plugin>:<server>; tools as mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__<tool>.
facts.limits: A local stdio server runs in Claude Code and in a desktop-app Cowork session, but NOT on claude.ai — reaching claude.ai users requires a remote https:// server instead. claude plugin validate's checks of .mcp.json entries (dropped-entry errors, unresolved ${user_config.KEY} refs, invalid remote URLs, non-loopback http/ws warnings, literal-credential-looking header warnings) require Claude Code v2.1.281 or later.

facts.behavior: Declared in .lsp.json at the plugin root (or the lspServers manifest key); gives Claude diagnostics and code navigation for a language via a language-server binary.
facts.limits: "claude plugin validate doesn't read this file" at all. An invalid entry only surfaces at session load time as "Invalid LSP server config for '.lsp.json'" in the /plugin Errors tab. When two enabled servers (from one or two plugins) claim the same file extension, the first registered wins and the other is unused for those files.

facts.behavior: output-styles/<name>.md and themes/<slug>.json ship reply-formatting styles and color themes that appear in the same /output-style and /theme pickers as the user's own.
facts.limits: Plugin themes are read-only: if a user edits one in /theme, the edit is saved as a copy in the user's own themes directory, not written back to the plugin.

facts.behavior: The workflows/ folder holds .js workflow files (a meta block plus a script that orchestrates subagents), runnable as /<plugin>:<name>.
facts.limits: The workflows manifest key REPLACES the default workflows/ folder scan rather than adding to it.

facts.behavior: A monitor is a shell command Claude Code runs as a persistent background process for the session; its output reaches Claude as notifications. Declared in monitors/monitors.json or experimental.monitors.
facts.limits: "Monitors run only in interactive sessions, and not on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, or Microsoft Foundry"; they never start in non-interactive (-p) mode. A monitor command can't reference ${user_config.*} — one that does simply never starts, and running monitor processes don't receive CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_<KEY> either. Disabling the plugin mid-session doesn't stop an already-running monitor; it stops only when the session ends.

facts.behavior: Files in bin/ at the plugin root are placed on the Bash tool's PATH while the plugin is enabled, so Claude can run them as bare commands with no separate install step.
facts.limits: Plugin bin/ directories come AFTER the user's own PATH entries, so a plugin cannot shadow git, ls, or other system commands. "claude.ai and Cowork don't install a plugin that has this directory" at all, including one distributed through claude.ai organization settings.

facts.feature: Default settings a plugin can ship (settings.json)
facts.behavior: A settings.json at the plugin root (or the settings manifest key) sets defaults applied while the plugin is enabled, so "a plugin can change how the session behaves and not only add components."
facts.limits: "Only two keys take effect from a plugin, agent and subagentStatusLine; every other key is dropped." When both settings.json and the manifest settings key are present, the file wins. Across sources, plugin defaults are the lowest layer — the user's own settings always override. When two enabled plugins set the same key, the plugin loaded last wins (logged as "overrides setting" under --debug).

facts.behavior: A channel lets an external system (e.g. a chat app) send messages into a session; declared as a channels manifest entry bound to one of the plugin's MCP servers, and can prompt for its own per-channel userConfig.
facts.limits: The channel entry's server field must match a key already declared in the plugin's mcpServers.

facts.behavior: Declares values (string/number/boolean/directory/file) Claude Code prompts the user for when the plugin is enabled, so users don't hand-edit settings.json; sensitive: true masks input and stores the value in the platform's secure credential store instead of settings.json.
facts.limits: The configuration dialog appears only in the interactive /plugin interface. "The claude plugin install shell command never prompts for userConfig values" — values must be passed as --config KEY=VALUE, or the install prints a "userConfig options not yet set" line. Each userConfig option object is strict: an unknown key inside it is an error and the plugin does not load (unlike an unrecognized top-level plugin.json field, which is merely stripped with a warning).

facts.behavior: Three variables plugin components reference: CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT (the installed version's absolute path), CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA (~/.claude/plugins/data/<id>/, persists across updates, for node_modules/caches), and CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR (the project root). Each is substituted only in specific documented fields (hook/monitor/MCP/LSP commands, skill/agent/command content) and exported to specific process types.
facts.limits: "The variables aren't present in the environment of commands Claude runs through the Bash tool, in the main session or in a subagent." CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT changes on every plugin update, so a plugin must not write persistent state there — CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA exists for that instead.

facts.behavior: The dependencies field (manifest or marketplace entry) lists other plugins that must be enabled for this one to work; bare names resolve against the plugin's own marketplace.
facts.limits: Enabling a plugin auto-enables its declared dependencies (failing if one is not installed or is blocked by org policy). Disabling a plugin that another enabled plugin depends on fails and names the dependents that must be disabled first.

facts.behavior: "Validate a plugin manifest, a marketplace manifest, or the skills, agents, and commands in a directory, and exit with a code a CI job can act on." Reports Validation passed / passed with warnings / failed (exit 0/0/1), plus exit 2 for an unexpected validator error. --strict treats warnings (e.g. unrecognized fields, missing metadata) as errors; --json emits a machine-readable report.
facts.limits: Given a directory it validates only one thing, by priority: marketplace.json, else plugin.json, else bare component files. It does not follow symlinks (warns instead), does not read a SKILL.md at the plugin root, and — critically — run against a MARKETPLACE directory it "doesn't open the plugins' skill, agent, command, or hook files, or the MCP server files they bundle"; each plugin directory must be validated separately to catch those. It also does not catch every failure: e.g. a marketplace entry's hooks written as a file path/array passes validation but silently never runs at load.

facts.feature: claude plugin details (component inventory and token cost)
facts.behavior: "Show a plugin's component inventory and projected token cost." Prints name/version/description/source, then Component inventory (skills, agents, hooks, MCP servers, LSP servers), Projected token cost (always-on tokens added to every session), and a Per-component always-on/on-invoke breakdown.
facts.limits: The plugin must already be loaded (installed, found in a skills directory, or passed via --plugin-dir/--plugin-url in the same command) — the command cannot inspect an arbitrary uninstalled plugin by name alone; for one that isn't loaded it prints "Plugin '<name>' not found..." and exits 1. Hooks and MCP servers get NO per-component cost row ("harness-only — no model context cost" / "tool schemas resolved at runtime; not counted"); MCP tool cost is only visible via /context in a live session. The command takes no flags beyond --help.

facts.behavior: "Every session where a plugin is enabled includes the names and descriptions of its skills, agents, and commands in Claude's context, and those tokens count against the user's usage whether or not the plugin gets used." The always-on figure counts each component's name plus its description and when_to_use frontmatter.
facts.limits: This applies per enabled plugin, every session, regardless of use — it is separate from on-invoke cost (the full skill/agent body, loaded only when that component actually runs). Reducing it (shortening descriptions, splitting a plugin) is left entirely to the plugin author; there is no automatic trimming.

facts.behavior: In /plugin, browsing a plugin from Anthropic's official marketplace shows a Context cost section with an "Every turn:" and a "When invoked:" line; the "Every turn:" line is visually highlighted once the always-on figure reaches 2,000 tokens or more.
facts.limits: "A plugin in your own marketplace has no Context cost section" — this pre-install estimate is exclusive to Anthropic's official marketplace listing, not third-party or self-hosted marketplaces.

facts.behavior: "A marketplace is a repository or directory with a .claude-plugin/marketplace.json file that lists plugins and where to fetch each one. It's a catalog, not a hosted store."
facts.limits: Claude Code adds Anthropic's official marketplace automatically on the first interactive terminal session (unless blocked by managed policy), but "adds no other marketplace on its own, including Anthropic's community and demo marketplaces."

facts.feature: Marketplace name tiers and reserved names
facts.behavior: Marketplace names fall into official / community / third-party tiers. A fixed list of names (claude-code-plugins, claude-plugins-official, claude-community, healthcare, anthropic-agent-skills, etc.) is reserved, and accepted only when the marketplace's source is github.com/anthropics/.
facts.limits: A name that impersonates an official marketplace (e.g. official-claude-plugins, a non-ASCII name) is refused outright at add time with "Marketplace name impersonates an official Anthropic/Claude marketplace"; if such a name is already registered, it and all its plugins stop loading. "npm", "pip", "uv", "cargo", "github", "gh", and names starting with "claudeai-" are also reserved in any casing.

facts.feature: Plugin source types (how a marketplace fetches a plugin)
facts.behavior: A plugin entry's source is one of: relative path (inside the marketplace), github (repo/ref/sha), url (any git URL), git-subdir (one subdirectory of another repo), npm (package/version/registry), archive (an https zip, optional sha256 pin), or command (a local command that prints the plugin directory's path).
facts.limits: npm sources fetch with install scripts explicitly disabled (no preinstall/postinstall). archive urls must be https and cannot target loopback, link-local, or cloud-metadata hosts. command sources cap the command string at 500 printable-ASCII characters with no run of 4+ spaces, and in copy mode cap the produced directory at 256 MiB / 20,000 entries; link mode is refused entirely on Windows. Relative-path sources only resolve when the marketplace itself was fetched as github/git/file/directory — not when the marketplace's own source type is url (only marketplace.json is fetched then).

facts.feature: Marketplace entry "strict" mode vs. a plugin's own plugin.json
facts.behavior: strict (default true) governs whether a marketplace entry may add components to a plugin that already ships its own plugin.json: with strict:true (default) the entry's commands/agents/skills/outputStyles/themes are appended to the manifest (hooks matchers replace the manifest's per event); with strict:false, an entry that sets any of those component fields is treated as a conflict.
facts.limits: "With strict: false, an entry that declares any component field is a conflict, and the plugin fails to load" with the message "Plugin <name> has conflicting manifests: both plugin.json and marketplace entry specify components." A marketplace entry's hooks must be written as an inline object — writing it as a file path or array passes claude plugin validate but the hooks silently never run at load ("not yet supported in a marketplace entry").

facts.behavior: Three scopes: user (enabled for you in every project on this computer), project (committed to .claude/settings.json, shared with collaborators who must still install locally themselves), and local (enabled for you in this repository only).
facts.limits: "A cloud session, including one in the browser at claude.ai/code, doesn't load the plugins in your local settings" at all, regardless of scope.

facts.feature: claude plugin install / enable / disable / update / uninstall
facts.behavior: install (alias i) and uninstall default to user scope; enable/disable auto-detect scope by checking local, then project, then user, in order, if --scope is omitted; update auto-detects across local, project, user, then managed.
facts.limits: Uninstalling a plugin from its LAST installed scope also deletes its stored userConfig options/secrets and its ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA} directory, unless --keep-data is passed. disable fails for a plugin another enabled plugin depends on, or one the organization requires as a synced plugin (org policy overrides a local disable attempt).

facts.behavior: Runs a plugin's eval cases (a prompt plus graders) several times in an isolated session with only the target plugin loaded, and by default also runs a no-plugin baseline arm for comparison. Requires Claude Code v2.1.269 or later.
facts.limits: "only evaluate plugins you trust — the run's sandboxing limits what a malicious plugin can reach but is not a guarantee, and a bundled suite passing is not a security vetting." The first run against an untrusted plugin directory asks the user to confirm before running (scaffold scripts and real MCP servers are opt-in); --trust-plugin answers that prompt for CI.

facts.behavior: Applies pending plugin changes (install, update, enable, disable, or on-disk edits made since session start) to a running session without restarting it, and prints a reload summary line with per-type counts.
facts.limits: When a reload would add/remove a plugin MCP server or the LSP tool in a way that would invalidate the prompt cache, Claude Code refuses to apply it automatically and requires an explicit /reload-plugins --force. In a non-interactive session (desktop app, Agent SDK, -p mode), the command only runs when typed directly into that session — when it arrives via Remote Control or a relayed Slack message, Claude Code replies it "isn't available over a remote connection in this session" and reloads nothing.

facts.behavior: A plugin the user installed from a marketplace moves under a "Not used recently" header in /plugin's Installed tab once unused for at least 14 days and 10 sessions; /skill-doctor flags skills (including plugin skills) that have never been invoked; /doctor lists unused plugins with a disable recommendation; /usage attributes recent usage share to plugins/skills/subagents/MCP servers.
facts.limits: The "Not used recently" header never appears for plugins loaded via --plugin-dir or a skills directory, enabled through managed settings, mounted from a seed directory, or that include a theme/output-style/monitor/workflow (those count as "in use" without a tracked invocation). It also never appears at all when the org sets strictKnownMarketplaces.

facts.feature: Plugin name field validation and component namespacing
facts.behavior: Every plugin component is namespaced under the manifest's name field, e.g. agent reviewer in plugin deploy-tools becomes deploy-tools:reviewer. name must contain no spaces, @, :, path separators, control characters, or bidirectional-formatting characters.
facts.limits: Using disallowed characters in name is a hard validation error. A name that isn't kebab-case is only a warning ("Validation passed with warnings"), not blocked, unless --strict is passed.

facts.feature: Unrecognized manifest fields (top-level vs. strict nested objects)
facts.behavior: An unrecognized top-level key in plugin.json is stripped and the plugin still loads, with claude plugin validate reporting it as a warning only. An unrecognized key inside a userConfig option, channels entry, lspServers config, or monitors entry is a hard error and the plugin does not load.
facts.limits: This distinction (lenient top level, strict nested objects) is specific to plugin.json; the same leniency applies to marketplace.json's own top-level and plugin-entry keys, which are also ignored-with-warning rather than rejected.

area: Claude Code native support for git and GitHub integration: commits, PR creation, the GitHub App and Actions integration, code review, branch handling, worktree branches (as of 2026-09-28)

facts.behavior: "Mention @claude in a pull request or issue comment to have Claude analyze code, implement changes, and push commits. You can also give the Claude Code GitHub Action a prompt to run automatically on any GitHub event. Use it to turn issues into pull requests, fix bugs from a comment, or automate recurring tasks."
facts.limits: Runs only inside a workflow file you (or /install-github-app) add to .github/workflows/; distinct from the managed Code Review service and from Claude Code in the cloud.

facts.behavior: "Claude Code installs the GitHub App, adds your authentication secret, and prepares the workflow pull request for you."
facts.limits: "works only with github.com repositories. If your repository's git remote is on gitlab.com or bitbucket.org, the command prints a notice and exits instead of starting setup." Requires admin access to the repo and the GitHub CLI (gh) installed and authenticated.

facts.behavior: "install the app, add the secret, and copy the workflow file into your repository yourself."
facts.limits: Used "when you don't run Claude Code locally, when the command fails, or when you want full control of the workflow files." Requires admin access to the repository.

facts.behavior: Installing grants a single fixed set: Actions RW, Checks RW, Contents RW, Discussions RW, Issues RW, Members R, Metadata R, Pull requests RW, Repository hooks RW, Statuses R, Workflows RW. "A GitHub App has a single permission set covering all of its features... When you install the app, you accept its full permission set. GitHub doesn't let you accept a subset."
facts.limits: A narrower custom app (Contents, Issues, Pull requests only) can be built instead, but "covers only the Claude Code GitHub Action. Code Review and web auto-fix still require the official app."

facts.behavior: "Interactive mode: when the workflow provides no prompt input, Claude waits for the trigger phrase, @claude by default, in an issue or pull request comment, in a pull request review, or in the body or title of a newly opened issue... Automation mode: when the workflow provides a prompt input, Claude runs without waiting for a mention."
facts.limits: Automation-mode results "appear in the workflow run log rather than a comment" by default; posting to the issue/PR requires the prompt to direct it and a tool that can post.

facts.behavior: "the Claude Code GitHub Action runs two checks on the triggering actor before Claude starts, and the run fails when either check rejects it: Write access... Human actor."
facts.limits: Write-access check is skipped for events no user authors (e.g. schedule). Bot actors are rejected unless listed in allowed_bots (including bot-attributed scheduled runs). Non-write users can be allowed only via allowed_non_write_users plus a custom github_token.

facts.behavior: "Claude skips draft and closed pull requests, pull requests it judges not to need a review, such as automated or trivial ones, and pull requests that already have a comment from Claude."
facts.limits: "On public repositories, GitHub withholds secrets from runs triggered by fork pull requests, so the review runs only on pull requests from branches in the same repository." Posting to the PR requires --comment plus an allowedTools rule naming the inline-comment MCP tool.

facts.feature: CI not triggering on Claude's Action commits
facts.behavior: "GitHub doesn't trigger workflows on commits made with the default GITHUB_TOKEN."
facts.limits: Only applies if the workflow passes github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}; fixed by authenticating as the Claude GitHub App (omit github_token) or passing a custom app token.

facts.behavior: "GitHub runs scheduled workflows only from the default branch and, in public repositories, disables the schedule after 60 days without repository activity."
facts.limits: Applies to schedule-triggered automation-mode runs specifically.

facts.feature: Tool access gating for plain-text automation prompts
facts.behavior: "For a plain-text prompt, Claude has no shell or GitHub API access until you grant the tools the prompt needs, with --allowedTools in claude_args or a permissions.allow rule in the settings input."
facts.limits: Skill-invoked prompts instead get tools from the skill's own allowed-tools frontmatter.

facts.feature: CLAUDE.md guidance for the GitHub Action
facts.behavior: "Create a CLAUDE.md file in your repository root to define code style guidelines, review criteria, project-specific rules, and preferred patterns. Claude follows these guidelines when creating PRs and responding to requests."
facts.limits: Best-practice guidance only; not independently enforced by the Action.

facts.behavior: "By default, the Claude Code GitHub Action calls the Claude API directly with your API key or OAuth token. To route inference through your own cloud account instead," set use_bedrock, use_vertex, or use_foundry; "you authenticate through OIDC identity federation instead of a Claude API key, so you store no static cloud credentials in your repository."
facts.limits: Three named providers only (Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry).

facts.feature: Creating pull requests from a session
facts.behavior: "You can create pull requests by asking Claude directly (\"create a pr for my changes\"), or guide Claude through it step-by-step." "Review Claude's generated PR before submitting and ask Claude to highlight potential risks or considerations."
facts.limits: Review before submitting is a stated tip, not an enforced gate.

facts.behavior: "Claude Code links the session to the PR when Claude creates it with gh pr create or glab mr create, and when Claude works on an existing PR." Retrieve with `claude --from-pr 1234` or by pasting the PR URL into the /resume picker search.
facts.limits: Automatic linking happens only via those two creation paths or when working an existing PR, not for a PR created by other means.

facts.behavior: "Each git worktree is a separate checkout on its own branch, created from an existing commit, so the repository needs at least one commit first." Example: `claude --worktree feature-auth`.
facts.limits: "In a repository with no commits, the command fails with Failed to resolve base branch \"HEAD\": git rev-parse failed."

facts.feature: Piping Claude into scripts (headless git usage)
facts.behavior: "Run Claude non-interactively for CI, pre-commit hooks, or batch processing. Stdin and stdout work like any Unix tool." Example: `git log --oneline -20 | claude -p "summarize these recent commits"`.
facts.limits: No git-specific enforcement described beyond general non-interactive/permission-flag behavior.

facts.behavior: Table entry: "GitHub Actions | Your CI pipeline | Tasks tied to repo events like opened PRs, or cron schedules that should live alongside your workflow config." Other rows: Routines (cloud), Desktop scheduled tasks (local machine), /loop (current CLI session).
facts.limits: Each option is scoped to a different execution environment; only GitHub Actions and Routines can trigger on GitHub events.

facts.feature: Code Review (managed cloud PR review service)
facts.behavior: "Code Review analyzes your GitHub pull requests and posts findings as inline comments on the lines of code where it found issues. A fleet of specialized agents examine the code changes in the context of your full codebase, looking for logic errors, security vulnerabilities, broken edge cases, and subtle regressions."
facts.limits: "is in research preview, available for Team and Enterprise subscriptions. It is not available for organizations with Zero Data Retention enabled." Reviews average 20 minutes and scale in cost with PR size.

facts.feature: Code Review findings do not gate merge
facts.behavior: "Findings are tagged by severity and don't approve or block your PR, so existing review workflows stay intact." "The check run always completes with a neutral conclusion so it never blocks merging through branch protection rules."
facts.limits: To gate merges on findings, a team must parse the check run's machine-readable severity summary in their own CI (via gh api + jq).

facts.behavior: 🔴 Important: "A bug that should be fixed before merging"; 🟡 Nit: "A minor issue, worth fixing but not blocking"; 🟣 Pre-existing: "A bug that exists in the codebase but was not introduced by this PR."
facts.limits: Severity is advisory metadata only; default calibration can be changed via REVIEW.md.

facts.feature: Code Review reactions/replies have no side effects
facts.behavior: "Replying to an inline comment does not prompt Claude to respond or update the PR." "Reactions do not trigger a re-review or change anything on the PR." "To dismiss a finding without a code change, resolve its thread; replying doesn't dismiss it."
facts.limits: Acting on a finding requires fixing the code and pushing (push-triggered mode) or commenting @claude review for a fresh review.

facts.behavior: "By default, Code Review focuses on correctness: bugs that would break production, not formatting preferences or missing test coverage. You can expand what it checks by adding guidance files to your repository."
facts.limits: Scope expansion requires CLAUDE.md/REVIEW.md; not configurable any other way.

facts.feature: Code Review setup requires org Owner
facts.behavior: "An Owner enables Code Review once for the organization and selects which repositories to include." Requires "the Owner or Primary Owner role in your Claude organization and permission to install GitHub Apps in your GitHub organization."
facts.limits: Per-repo enablement is chosen during this org-level setup; individual contributors cannot self-enable it.

facts.behavior: Three settings per repository: "Once after PR creation" (runs once on open/ready-for-review); "After every push" ("catching new issues as the PR evolves and auto-resolving threads when you fix flagged issues"); "Manual" (comment @claude review to request one, or @claude review always to subscribe).
facts.limits: "Whichever option you choose, Claude reviews a pull request from a fork only when someone comments @claude review on it."

facts.feature: Fork pull requests excluded from automatic Code Review
facts.behavior: "Claude doesn't review a pull request from a fork automatically, regardless of the repository's Review Behavior setting. To start one, comment @claude review on the pull request." "Clicking Re-run on the check run doesn't start a review" and "Pushing new commits doesn't start a review, even in a repository set to After every push."
facts.limits: The write access required to trigger is to the base repository, not the fork.

facts.behavior: Table: `@claude review` "Starts a single review without subscribing the PR to future pushes"; `@claude review always` "Starts a review and subscribes the PR to push-triggered reviews going forward"; `@claude review once` "Same as @claude review."
facts.limits: Must be "a top-level PR comment, not an inline comment on a diff line"; command must lead the comment; requires write/maintain/admin permission on the repo; PR must be open; a private org membership can block eligibility unless added as a direct collaborator. Manual triggers, unlike automatic ones, do run on draft PRs.

facts.behavior: "Code Review reads your repository's CLAUDE.md files and treats newly introduced violations as nit-level findings. This works bidirectionally: if your PR changes code in a way that makes a CLAUDE.md statement outdated, Claude flags that the docs need updating too." "Claude reads CLAUDE.md files at every level of your directory hierarchy, so rules in a subdirectory's CLAUDE.md apply only to files under that path."
facts.limits: Violations are capped at nit severity by default (not escalated without REVIEW.md).

facts.behavior: "REVIEW.md is a file at your repository root that tailors Code Review to your repo. The agents in the review pipeline that find and verify findings receive its contents as your repository's review instructions... and the agents that rank and report findings consult it before settling severity and writing the review." Supports redefining severity, capping nit volume, skip rules, repo-specific checks, a verification bar, re-review convergence rules, and summary shape.
facts.limits: Used only by the managed cloud Code Review service; "the [local /code-review] review follows your CLAUDE.md like any Claude Code session, but it doesn't read REVIEW.md."

facts.feature: Code Review pricing and spend cap
facts.behavior: "Code Review is billed based on token usage. Each review averages $15-25 in cost... billed separately through usage credits and does not count against your plan's included usage." "To set a monthly spend cap for Code Review, go to claude.ai/admin-settings/usage."
facts.limits: When the cap is reached: "Code Review posts a single comment on the PR explaining that the review was skipped. Reviews resume automatically at the start of the next billing period, or immediately when an admin raises the cap."

facts.behavior: "Review runs are best-effort, and a failed run never blocks your PR. Code Review retries some interrupted reviews on its own."
facts.limits: Manual retrigger via an @claude review comment, or the check's Re-run button (non-fork PRs only).

facts.behavior: "The /code-review command reviews a diff in your terminal without installing the GitHub App. It reports correctness bugs and reuse, simplification, and efficiency cleanups." "It reviews your branch's commits ahead of its upstream plus any uncommitted changes, so it needs work on the branch or in the working tree to have something to report." Accepts a target: file path, PR number, branch name, or ref range like main...my-feature.
facts.limits: /review is now an alias of /code-review (before v2.1.223 it was a separate, single-pass read-only PR review command). Requires no GitHub App install, unlike managed Code Review.

facts.behavior: "--fix: applies the findings to your working tree after the review." "--comment: posts the findings on a GitHub pull request as inline comments, or on a GitLab merge request as a single note." "--post: on an ultra cloud review of a github.com pull request, preselects posting the finished findings to the PR in the launch dialog... Requires Claude Code v2.1.227 or later."
facts.limits: GitLab posting via --comment requires the glab CLI (v2.1.257+); without it, "Claude prints the findings in the terminal instead."

facts.behavior: "Pass an effort level to trade coverage for confidence. At low and medium, the review reports only the findings it's most confident in... high through max broaden coverage and may include findings the review is less sure about." "When you don't type a level, the review reuses the last level from low through max you typed, even in an earlier session."
facts.limits: `ultra` "neither updates nor uses the remembered level"; a level passed in a non-interactive -p run doesn't update the remembered level either.

facts.behavior: "The review runs in the background by default... It runs in the foreground instead" when re-run while a prior review is in progress, in non-interactive (-p/SDK) mode, or when CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1.
facts.limits: "A background review applies its --fix edits outside your session's checkpoints... so /rewind doesn't undo them; use git to revert them." Foreground-run edits are restored by /rewind as usual.

facts.behavior: "Claude can start /code-review on its own. Ask it to review your changes in plain language and it can run the skill without you typing the command, and a scheduled task with /code-review as its prompt runs the review." "A scheduled task never launches the cloud review, so schedule /code-review without the ultra argument."
facts.limits: To prevent self-start while keeping it user-invocable, set `"skillOverrides": {"code-review": "user-invocable-only"}` in a settings file (e.g. ~/.claude/settings.json). Before v2.1.246 self-start was gated behind a remote feature flag.

facts.behavior: "/code-review ultra --fix runs the deeper ultrareview in the cloud, then applies its findings to your working tree when they arrive back in your session." "Ultrareview uses its own scope: your current branch against the repository's default branch, plus uncommitted and staged changes in the working tree."
facts.limits: "requires authentication with a claude.ai account and is not available on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, or Microsoft Foundry, or to organizations with Zero Data Retention enabled. When ultrareview is not available, /code-review ultra runs a local review in your session instead." Billing confirmation needs an interactive session (use the `claude ultrareview` subcommand for non-interactive use with explicit consent).

facts.behavior: "Run ultrareview non-interactively. Prints findings to stdout and exits 0 on success or 1 on failure." Flags: --json (raw payload), --timeout <minutes> (overrides a 45-minute default), --post (post findings as a comment on a github.com PR target; default is --no-post).
facts.limits: Requires Claude Code v2.1.218 or later for the non-interactive launch path.

facts.behavior: Removal of a background session "is refused over the session's worktree" by default; a second `claude rm` with an explicit flag resolves it: `--discard-unpushed <commit>@<worktree-id>` "discards a worktree that has unpushed commits along with those commits" (requires v2.1.260+); `--force-remove-worktree <worktree-id>` "deletes a worktree directory that git or the WorktreeRemove hook couldn't remove" (requires v2.1.268+).
facts.limits: "The conversation transcript stays on your local machine, available through claude --resume" even after the worktree is discarded.

facts.behavior: "Open the session picker filtered to sessions linked to a specific pull request. Accepts a PR number, a GitHub or GitHub Enterprise PR URL, a GitLab merge request URL, or a Bitbucket pull request URL. Sessions are linked automatically when Claude creates the pull request."
facts.limits: Only finds sessions Claude Code already linked (via gh pr create / glab mr create, or working an existing PR).

facts.behavior: Git Bash invocations can be allow- or deny-listed by pattern, e.g. `Bash(git log *)`, `Bash(git diff *)`, so specific git subcommands run without a permission prompt or are denied outright.
facts.limits: A scoped disallow rule leaves the tool available generally and denies only calls that match the pattern as written.

facts.behavior: "In a host application that requests the findings list, such as the desktop app, Claude reports the review's findings through the ReportFindings tool instead. Claude Code renders the report as a findings list, and each entry shows the file location, a one-sentence summary, and a category tag such as correctness when the finding carries one."
facts.limits: "A host request applies at every effort level and requires Claude Code v2.1.218 or later." In a terminal session or a `-p` run with text/JSON output, findings are reported as text instead, even when the host requests a list.

facts.feature: Findings status tracking across a session
facts.behavior: "When Claude fixes reported findings later in the session, it reports them again, and Claude Code marks each finding in the updated findings list as fixed, skipped, or no change needed."
facts.limits: Scoped to the same session that produced the original findings list.

area: Claude Code native support for sessions/resume, worktrees and their cleanup, sandboxing, checkpointing, background tasks, and what carries between sessions (as of 2026-09-28)

facts.behavior: Sessions are saved continuously to local transcript files as you work, so you can return to one after exiting or running /clear.
facts.limits: Applies to interactive sessions and claude -p runs by default; suppressed for one print run by --no-session-persistence, or globally by CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY.

facts.behavior: Reopens the most recent conversation in the current directory.
facts.limits: Skips claude -p/Agent SDK sessions (unless -p is also passed) and sessions whose first prompt was /loop; opens a finished background session but not one that is still running.

facts.behavior: Resumes a specific session by session ID, name, or transcript path; --resume with no argument opens an interactive picker.
facts.limits: Session-ID lookup checks the current project/worktrees first, then every other project on the machine, but resolves cross-project only when exactly one other project holds a transcript with messages for that ID.

facts.behavior: Opens the session picker filtered to sessions linked to a given pull/merge request number, URL, or search term.
facts.limits: Only finds sessions that were already linked to that PR.

facts.behavior: Restores full conversation history (including tool calls/results), the model, the agent, permission mode (with documented exceptions), an active goal, unexpired scheduled tasks, and shows unfinished background work as a note Claude reads with the next prompt.
facts.limits: A tool still running when the process ended does not finish or auto-rerun; the model isn't restored if retired/disallowed or overridden by launch flags; background Bash/monitor tasks are never restored; expired scheduled tasks are dropped.

facts.feature: Config flags not restored on resume
facts.behavior: --mcp-config, --settings, --plugin-dir, --fallback-model, and --add-dir directories must be passed again when resuming; standard settings files (settings.json etc.) are re-read automatically so they don't need re-passing.
facts.limits: Directories added mid-session with /add-dir also aren't restored, though the picker still uses them to locate the session.

facts.behavior: Which permission mode a resumed session starts in depends on the resume path (terminal, non-interactive -p, VS Code, session picker, /resume) and the mode the session ended in, per a documented table.
facts.limits: The session picker, /resume with an argument, and most non-interactive resumes do not restore the stored permission mode; plan mode is the main mode restored across -p and VS Code resumes.

facts.behavior: On Pro/Max, resuming a session inactive for over ~1 hour and above 100,000 tokens opens a dialog offering to resume from a /compact summary, resume the full session as-is, or stop asking.
facts.limits: Only triggers once the conversation's prompt cache has expired; the next request reprocesses the full history once regardless of which option is picked.

facts.behavior: By default the picker shows sessions from the current worktree plus sessions started elsewhere that added the current directory with /add-dir; Ctrl+W widens to all worktrees of the repo, Ctrl+A to every project on the machine.
facts.limits: Sessions whose first prompt was /loop never appear in the picker, even though they still exist and can be resumed by ID.

facts.behavior: Sessions can be named at startup (-n), mid-session (/rename), from the picker (Ctrl+R), or receive an auto-generated title from the first prompt or an accepted plan.
facts.limits: Only a set name or a generated/plan title works as a resume handle; the default display name (e.g. my-app-3f) shown in listings is not a resume handle.

facts.behavior: Creates a copy of the conversation so far and switches into it, leaving the original untouched; conversation history, in-session 'allow' permission grants, in-flight background subagents/Bash, and any Remote Control connection all carry into the branch.
facts.limits: --fork-session instead starts a genuinely separate process that does not inherit in-session permission grants, which must be re-approved.

facts.behavior: Starts a fresh, empty context; Claude Code saves the previous conversation so it can be resumed via /resume or the rewind menu's previous-session entry.
facts.limits: The rewind-menu shortcut to the pre-clear conversation is available only until you exit Claude Code or resume a different session.

facts.behavior: /export renders the current conversation to clipboard or a text file for a person to read; scripts instead use claude -p --output-format json/stream-json, claude -p --resume for follow-up queries, the hook transcript_path field, or the Agent SDK.
facts.limits: The raw .jsonl transcript entry format is internal and changes between versions, so scripts should not parse it directly.

facts.behavior: Transcripts are stored as JSONL at ~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-id>.jsonl, one JSON object per message/tool-use/metadata entry, with <project> derived from the working-directory path.
facts.limits: Storage root is movable with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR; project directory naming can be overridden with CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME (requires CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR to also be set).

facts.behavior: A retention sweep deletes session data once it exceeds the cleanupPeriodDays setting, default 30 days.
facts.limits: Desktop/Cowork transcripts use a separate desktopSessionCleanupPeriodDays setting and are otherwise kept indefinitely; deleting a background session with claude rm keeps its transcript resumable via claude --resume.

facts.behavior: Deletes a project's transcripts and related state on demand, sooner than the retention sweep would.
facts.limits: Does not affect prompt history (history.jsonl) or configuration files (CLAUDE.md, settings.json, skills, agents, etc.).

facts.behavior: Creates an isolated worktree under .claude/worktrees/<name>/ at the repository root, on a new branch named worktree-<name>, and starts Claude in it.
facts.limits: Requires a git repository (or a WorktreeCreate hook for other VCS); interactive runs require prior workspace trust, or the flag exits with an error.

facts.behavior: Mid-session, Claude can create or switch into a worktree by calling the EnterWorktree tool, and leave one with ExitWorktree.
facts.limits: Entering a path outside the repo's .claude/worktrees/ requires explicit user approval that cannot be suppressed by a permission rule or 'don't ask again,' only by bypassPermissions mode.

facts.behavior: On exit, Claude checks the worktree for changed/untracked files, uncommitted submodule work, and new commits; a clean unnamed-session worktree and its branch are removed automatically, while a named or dirty worktree prompts to keep or remove.
facts.limits: Non-interactive (-p) runs get no exit prompt and never clean up their worktrees; the creation-time lock on them is released only later, by the periodic stale-lock sweep.

facts.behavior: While a session is isolated in a worktree, Claude Code blocks Edit/Write/NotebookEdit that target the main checkout, Bash/PowerShell/Monitor commands whose working directory resolves to the main checkout, git redirects into the main checkout, and any command whose git-safety can't be verified from its text alone.
facts.limits: The command-shape check cannot be turned off; PowerShell only gets the working-directory check; the checks cover the launching repo and the main checkout a linked worktree links from, and apply to every subagent the isolated session spawns.

facts.behavior: A subagent definition can set isolation: worktree in its frontmatter (or be asked ad hoc) to always run in its own temporary worktree, branched from the same base as --worktree.
facts.limits: Claude Code removes a finished subagent's worktree automatically only if it made no changes; one with changes stays on disk until the periodic sweep can remove it without losing work.

facts.behavior: A periodic sweep removes worktrees Claude created for subagents and background sessions once they are older than cleanupPeriodDays, under the same retention sweep rules as other Claude Code data.
facts.limits: The sweep leaves in place any worktree with changed/untracked files, unpushed commits, an uninspectable or dirty submodule, one belonging to an un-backgrounded --worktree session (whatever its age), or one the user created themselves with git worktree add.

facts.behavior: Controls whether new worktrees branch from the repository's default branch on the remote ("fresh", the default) or from the current local HEAD ("head", carrying unpushed commits).
facts.limits: Cannot be set to an arbitrary branch name; branching from a specific existing branch requires creating the worktree with git directly.

facts.behavior: A gitignore-syntax file at the project root that copies listed gitignored files (e.g. .env) into every new worktree Claude Code creates with git, so a fresh checkout still has local config.
facts.limits: Not processed when a WorktreeCreate hook replaces the default git-based worktree creation; only files that both match a pattern and are gitignored are copied, so tracked files are never duplicated.

facts.feature: What worktrees share with the main checkout
facts.behavior: Worktrees share the repository's .git directory, project-scope plugins, saved 'don't ask again' permission approvals (written to the main checkout's .claude/settings.local.json and applying to every worktree), and, when a worktree has no own .claude/skills (or agents/commands) directory, read-through access to the main checkout's copies.
facts.limits: On Windows and other cases where Claude Code doesn't use the repository root, a permission approval stays scoped to that one worktree instead of the main checkout.

facts.behavior: Worktrees can be created, listed, and removed directly with git worktree add/list/remove, e.g. to check out a specific existing branch or place a worktree outside the repository.
facts.limits: Bypasses Claude Code's own creation defaults, including the base-branch setting, .worktreeinclude, and its filter-driver neutralization.

facts.behavior: For SVN, Perforce, Mercurial, or other non-git VCS, WorktreeCreate and WorktreeRemove hooks replace the default git-based worktree logic entirely, including where worktrees are placed.
facts.limits: .worktreeinclude is not processed when a hook replaces the git logic; the hook's created directory must sit outside any git repository, or the isolation-safety check refuses to adopt it.

facts.behavior: Sandboxed commands run under operating-system-enforced boundaries (Seatbelt on macOS, bubblewrap on Linux/WSL2) that define which files and network domains a Bash, PowerShell, or Monitor command and its child processes can touch, instead of stopping to ask permission for each one.
facts.limits: Native Windows is not supported (must run under WSL2); the sandbox isolates only Bash-family subprocesses, never the built-in Read/Edit/Write tools or computer use.

facts.behavior: Auto-allow mode runs sandboxable commands automatically without a permission prompt because the OS boundary contains them; regular-permissions mode keeps the normal prompt flow even for sandboxed commands.
facts.limits: Even in auto-allow, explicit deny rules, rm/rmdir on a critical path, content-scoped ask rules (e.g. Bash(git push *)), and plan mode still force a prompt.

facts.behavior: When a command can't run inside the sandbox (incompatible tool, disallowed host), Claude may retry it with the dangerouslyDisableSandbox parameter, which runs it outside the sandbox through the regular permission flow.
facts.limits: Can be disabled entirely with sandbox.allowUnsandboxedCommands: false, after which every Claude-run command must run sandboxed unless explicitly listed in excludedCommands; typed !-prefixed shell-mode commands run outside the sandbox regardless, except in background sessions or with CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB set.

facts.behavior: By default sandboxed commands can read the entire computer except denied paths, but can write only to the current working directory, directories added with --add-dir/permissions.additionalDirectories, and a per-user temp directory.
facts.limits: Default read access still includes credential files such as ~/.aws/credentials and ~/.ssh/ unless explicitly blocked via sandbox.credentials or denyRead; can be disabled entirely (filesystem.disabled) while network isolation stays on, but only from user/managed/--settings sources, not project settings.

facts.behavior: Even inside directories a sandboxed command can otherwise write to, the sandbox still denies writes to Claude Code's own config/code paths: .claude settings/skills/agents/commands/hooks, .mcp.json, shell startup files, git internals (in the working directory), and most of ~/.claude, so a running command can't grant itself permissions or plant a hook/MCP server that runs outside the sandbox.
facts.limits: No allowWrite entry or Edit allow rule can exempt one of these paths; the only way to turn the protection off is filesystem.disabled, which disables the whole filesystem layer, not just this list.

facts.behavior: Network access goes through a proxy outside the sandbox; no domains are pre-allowed by default, the first command needing a new domain prompts for approval (or the classifier reviews named hosts in auto mode), and 'Yes, and don't ask again' saves a WebFetch(domain:...) rule for future sessions.
facts.limits: By default the built-in proxy does not terminate or inspect TLS, so it enforces the allowlist by requested hostname only and cannot see encrypted contents; without a custom TLS-terminating proxy, domain fronting or similar techniques could reach hosts outside the allowlist through an allowed broad domain.

facts.behavior: The sandbox.credentials setting declares credential files and environment variables to deny (block reads / unset the variable) or mask (show a sentinel to the command; the proxy substitutes the real value only on egress to allowed hosts) for sandboxed commands.
facts.limits: There is no built-in credential deny list, only what you explicitly list; mask entries, network.tlsTerminate, and credentials.allowPlaintextInject are honored only from user settings, managed settings, or --settings, never from a repository's own .claude/settings.json or settings.local.json.

facts.behavior: If sandbox dependencies are missing or the platform is unsupported, Claude Code by default shows a warning and runs commands without sandboxing; sandbox.failIfUnavailable makes that a hard startup failure instead, intended for managed deployments that require sandboxing as a security gate.
facts.limits: The default behavior silently downgrades to no isolation rather than blocking, so sandboxing is not guaranteed on by default even when enabled, unless failIfUnavailable is also set.

facts.feature: Sandbox scope (Bash-family only) and relation to permissions
facts.behavior: Sandboxing restricts what an already-approved shell command can access at the OS level; permission rules and permission modes separately decide whether a tool call runs at all and whether you're prompted, and apply to every tool (Bash, Read, Edit, WebFetch, MCP, etc.), not just Bash.
facts.limits: Effective sandboxing requires both filesystem and network isolation together; widening one (a broad allowWrite path, a broad allowedDomains entry, an excludedCommands exception) without checking the other can undo the intended protection.

facts.behavior: Claude Code automatically tracks file edits made by Claude's file-editing tools and captures a checkpoint of code state before every prompt that starts a new turn.
facts.limits: Keeps file snapshots for only the 100 most recent checkpoints in a session; discarding an older checkpoint deletes snapshot files no remaining checkpoint references (except each file's very first snapshot, kept as the VS Code extension's diff baseline).

facts.behavior: Opens a menu (or double-Esc on an empty prompt) listing each prompt sent in the session, letting you restore code and/or conversation to that point, or summarize the conversation from or up to it.
facts.limits: The two code-restore options appear only when the selected checkpoint actually has tracked file changes to revert; messages that joined a running turn via queueing are not listed as separate checkpoints.

facts.behavior: Checkpoints are saved with the conversation, so /rewind still works after resuming a session; Claude Code deletes a session's file snapshots in the retention sweep, by default about 30 days after the session last saved one (via cleanupPeriodDays).
facts.limits: Rewinding to a checkpoint whose snapshots have already been swept can fail with a 'No files were restored' error.

facts.feature: Checkpointing limitation: Bash-modified files not tracked
facts.behavior: Checkpointing does not track files modified by Bash commands such as rm, mv, or cp; only direct edits made through Claude's file-editing tools are tracked and can be undone via rewind.
facts.limits: File deletions, renames, or copies performed by shell commands cannot be undone through /rewind at all.

facts.feature: Checkpointing limitation: subagent edits not restored
facts.behavior: A subagent's file edits are usually not captured in the parent session's checkpoints; whether /rewind restores them depends on how the subagent ran.
facts.limits: Only a foreground-run forked skill's edits are restored by rewind; edits from any other subagent — including a background-run forked skill and a background /code-review --fix run — require git to revert instead.

facts.behavior: Checkpointing only tracks files edited within the current session; manual edits made outside Claude Code, and edits from other concurrent sessions, are normally not captured.
facts.limits: They are captured only incidentally, if they happen to modify the same files the current session also edits.

facts.behavior: When restoring code, Claude Code skips any tracked path that is a symlink or hard link and shows a 'Restored the code, but skipped N files' warning; the skipped files keep their current contents rather than being reverted.
facts.limits: Covers, for example, dotfile-manager-symlinked config files and pnpm hard-linked files; those must be reverted manually or by asking Claude to reverse the edit.
