facts.behavior: The documentation states checkpoints are designed for quick, session-level recovery, and directs users to continue using git for permanent version history and collaboration.
facts.limits: Not a substitute for commits, branches, or long-term history.

facts.behavior: Claude Code can run a Bash command asynchronously in the background (by prompting Claude, or pressing Ctrl+B), returning a task ID immediately and writing output to a file Claude reads via the Read tool while continuing to respond to new prompts.
facts.limits: Auto-terminated if output exceeds 5GB; on macOS/Linux, stopped under critical memory pressure only once the session has been idle 30+ minutes with no turn or subagent running (disable via CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BG_SHELL_PRESSURE_REAP); a command that hits its timeout is auto-moved to the background instead of stopped, unless it starts with sleep.

facts.behavior: Background tasks are automatically cleaned up when Claude Code exits; on macOS and Linux, stopping a task from /tasks or at exit also stops processes that detached from the task's shell (e.g. under setsid or timeout).
facts.limits: If you background the whole session rather than exiting, its background tasks keep running in that background session instead of being cleaned up.

facts.behavior: An environment variable that disables all background-Bash-task functionality when set to 1.
facts.limits: Governs background Bash commands specifically, not background sessions (agent view).

facts.behavior: Full Claude Code conversations that keep running without a terminal attached, hosted by a supervisor process; created via claude agents, claude --bg, /background (/bg), or /fork, and managed with claude attach/logs/stop/rm/respawn/agents --json.
facts.limits: Each background session consumes subscription quota independently of others; sessions on third-party model providers use that provider's own quota.

facts.behavior: A background session starts in the working directory, then moves into its own isolated worktree at .claude/worktrees/<session-id>/ before editing files, so parallel background sessions read the same checkout but each writes to its own worktree.
facts.limits: Isolation is skipped when already inside a linked worktree, when the working directory isn't a git repository and no WorktreeCreate hook is configured, or for a write outside the working directory; can be turned off entirely with worktree.bgIsolation: "none" (documented as not recommended for parallel sessions).

facts.feature: Deleting a background session (claude rm / Ctrl+X twice)
facts.behavior: Deleting a session removes it from the list and, when safe, removes its worktree too; whether the worktree is kept depends on whether it has uncommitted changes, unpushed commits, is in use by another session, or was created by the user directly.
facts.limits: A worktree with unpushed commits is kept unless --discard-unpushed is passed; a worktree the user created themselves (git worktree add) is always left in place regardless of flags.

facts.feature: Background session state persistence across stop/restart
facts.behavior: When a background session is stopped and later restarted (claude respawn), its permission mode, model, effort level, config flags (--mcp-config, --settings, --add-dir, --fallback-model), added directories, and session name all persist.
facts.limits: Documented specifically for background sessions; this list differs from what a plain interactive --resume restores per the sessions.md table.

facts.behavior: Claude automatically creates and maintains per-project memory files under ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/ (an index MEMORY.md plus topic files), read at session start and pulled in on demand — the main mechanism by which context carries between otherwise-separate sessions on a project.
facts.limits: Not deleted by the age-based retention sweep except when the whole memory directory stays empty for the entire retention period; on by default, toggled with /memory or the autoMemoryEnabled setting; the user never writes these files directly.

facts.behavior: Claude Code keeps a history of typed prompts, stored per working directory, reachable via Up-arrow recall and Ctrl+R reverse search across past sessions of the same project.
facts.limits: Per the claude-directory reference, this history file is not subject to the age-based cleanup sweep and is kept until manually deleted, unlike most session data.

facts.behavior: Claude's task checklist persists across context compactions within a session; setting CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID lets a named task list be shared across multiple sessions.
facts.limits: The list fills only in sessions whose model has task-tracking tools by default, or that opt in with CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1; on any other model it stays empty.

facts.behavior: When a claude.ai usage limit stops Claude mid-task, Claude Code by default waits in the open interactive session and automatically continues the task once the limit resets, sending a fixed continuation prompt rather than resending the last message.
facts.limits: On by default only for interactive sessions signed in with a claude.ai subscription; not offered at all for background sessions or -p runs, API keys, usage-based billing, or an LLM gateway without a saved claude.ai login; re-arms itself automatically at most twice before stopping.

facts.behavior: Bypasses all permission checks for the session, or (the --allow- form) makes that bypass available as an option without turning it on by default.
facts.limits: CLI help text recommends it only for sandboxes with no internet access; it is blocked outright when Claude Code runs as root or via sudo on Linux/macOS, unless running inside a recognized sandbox.

facts.behavior: Removes the built-in tools that run commands or code (Bash, PowerShell, REPL, etc.) and WebFetch unless named via --tools, ignores user/project/local settings files, confines file tools to the working directories, and refuses bypassPermissions.
facts.limits: Managed settings and --settings still apply; MCP servers still load unless --strict-mcp-config is also passed.

facts.behavior: A minimal mode that skips hooks (user-defined ones; built-in Claude Code features are unaffected), LSP, plugin sync, attribution, auto-memory, background prefetches, keychain reads, and CLAUDE.md auto-discovery; sets CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE=1.
facts.limits: Skills still resolve via /skill-name; context (CLAUDE.md dirs, MCP config, etc.) must be supplied explicitly through flags since auto-discovery is off.

facts.behavior: Starts a session with all customizations disabled — CLAUDE.md, skills, installed plugins, hooks, MCP servers, custom commands/agents, output styles, workflows, custom themes, and keybindings — for troubleshooting a broken configuration; sets CLAUDE_CODE_SAFE_MODE=1.
facts.limits: Admin-managed (policy) settings still apply; auth, model selection, built-in tools/plugins, and permissions work normally.

facts.behavior: Lets the caller assign a specific UUID as the session ID for a new conversation instead of Claude Code generating one.
facts.limits: The value must be a valid UUID.

facts.behavior: Creates a tmux session for the worktree, using iTerm2-native panes when available, or classic tmux with --tmux=classic.
facts.limits: Requires --worktree to be passed in the same invocation.

area: Checkpointing and rewind of file edits in Claude Code (as of 2026-09-28)

facts.behavior: "Claude Code automatically tracks Claude's file edits as you work" and "checkpointing automatically captures the state of your code before each prompt you send that starts a turn." "Every prompt you send that starts a turn creates a new checkpoint."
facts.limits: Only captures state before prompts that start a new turn; a queued message that joins an already-running turn does not get its own checkpoint (see separate fact).

facts.behavior: "Claude Code keeps file snapshots for the 100 most recent checkpoints in a session. Discarding an older checkpoint deletes the snapshot files that no remaining checkpoint references, except each file's first snapshot, which the VS Code extension uses as the baseline for its session diffs."
facts.limits: Applies per session; checkpoints beyond the 100 most recent have their snapshot files discarded (except each file's first snapshot, kept for VS Code extension diff baselines).

facts.behavior: "Claude Code saves checkpoints with the conversation, so you can still run /rewind after you resume a session."
facts.limits: None stated beyond the retention sweep deletion (separate fact).

facts.feature: Retention sweep deletes old snapshots (default ~30 days)
facts.behavior: "Claude Code deletes a session's file snapshots in the retention sweep, by default about 30 days after the session last saved one. Rewinding to a checkpoint whose snapshots are gone can fail with No files were restored. To keep snapshots longer, set cleanupPeriodDays."
facts.limits: Default ~30-day window; configurable via the cleanupPeriodDays setting (see settings-reference). Rewinding to a checkpoint past this window can fail outright.

facts.feature: /rewind command and Esc-Esc shortcut open the rewind menu
facts.behavior: "Run /rewind, or press Esc twice when the prompt input is empty, to open the rewind menu." If the prompt input contains text, double Esc clears it instead of opening the menu (cleared text is saved to input history, recallable with Up).
facts.limits: Esc-Esc only opens the menu when the prompt input is empty; otherwise it just clears text.

facts.feature: Rewind menu lists prompts, with an exclusion
facts.behavior: "The rewind menu lists each prompt you sent during the session, except messages that joined a running turn."
facts.limits: Mid-turn queued messages that joined a running turn are not listed as separate rewind points (see mid-turn fact).

facts.behavior: Selecting a point offers: "Restore code and conversation: revert both code and conversation to that point"; "Restore conversation: rewind to that message while keeping current code"; "Restore code: revert file changes while keeping the conversation"; "Summarize from here: compress the conversation from this point forward into a summary, freeing context window space"; "Summarize up to here: compress the conversation before this point into a summary, keeping later messages intact"; "Never mind: return to the message list without making changes."
facts.limits: The two code-restore options (Restore code and conversation; Restore code) appear only when the selected checkpoint has tracked file changes to revert; otherwise only Restore conversation, the summarize options, and Never mind are offered.

facts.feature: Rewind past a cleared conversation (/clear interaction)
facts.behavior: "If you ran /clear earlier in the same Claude Code process, the rewind menu shows an additional entry at the top of the list labeled /resume <session-id> (previous session). Select it to resume the conversation that was active before /clear ran."
facts.limits: "The entry is available until you exit Claude Code or resume a different session."

facts.feature: Guided summarization does not touch disk
facts.behavior: "Summarizing doesn't change files on disk, and the original messages stay in the session transcript, so Claude can still reference the details." Instructions can be typed to guide what a Summarize option focuses on.
facts.limits: Summarize is conversation/context-only; it never reverts or modifies files. Distinct from /branch or claude --continue --fork-session, which preserve the original session while branching off.

facts.feature: Limitation: Bash command file changes are not tracked
facts.behavior: "Checkpointing does not track files modified by Bash commands." Example given: rm file.txt, mv old.txt new.txt, cp source.txt dest.txt. "These file modifications cannot be undone through rewind. Only direct file edits made through Claude's file editing tools are tracked."
facts.limits: Scope is limited to Claude's file editing tools (Edit/Write-type tools); any file mutation via Bash (delete, move, copy, etc.) is outside checkpointing's tracking and cannot be restored by /rewind.

facts.feature: Limitation: subagent edits are usually not restored
facts.behavior: "A subagent makes edits with Claude's file editing tools, but Claude Code usually doesn't capture those edits in your session's checkpoints." Exception: "Foreground forked skill: a skill with context: fork that runs in the foreground edits your working tree during your own turn, so rewinding restores its edits as usual." "Any other subagent: rewinding doesn't restore the edits. Use git to revert them. This includes a forked skill that runs in the background, the default, and a background /code-review --fix run."
facts.limits: Only foreground forked skills (context: fork, background: false, or situations that force foreground per the skills page) have their edits captured by checkpointing. Background subagents' edits, including background /code-review --fix, are not restorable via /rewind and must be reverted with git instead.

facts.feature: Limitation: external/out-of-session changes are not tracked
facts.behavior: "Checkpointing only tracks files that have been edited within the current session. Manual changes you make to files outside of Claude Code and edits from other concurrent sessions are normally not captured, unless they happen to modify the same files as the current session."
facts.limits: Scope is the current session only; manual edits and edits from other concurrent Claude Code sessions fall outside tracking unless they happen to touch files the current session also tracks.

facts.feature: Limitation: messages sent mid-turn are not checkpointed
facts.behavior: "When a message you queue while Claude works reaches Claude within the running turn, it joins that turn instead of starting a new one. The message appears in the conversation, but Claude Code doesn't create a checkpoint for it, and the rewind menu doesn't list it." "To remove such a message, or undo the edits Claude made after it, rewind to the prompt that started the turn. That rewinds the whole turn, including the work Claude did before your message arrived."
facts.limits: A queued message that Claude Code sends as part of a new turn does get a checkpoint as usual (including when several queued messages share that turn); only messages that join an already-running turn are exempt.

facts.feature: Limitation: symlinked and hard-linked paths are not restored
facts.behavior: "Checkpointing doesn't rewind symlinked or hard-linked files. When you pick Restore code or Restore code and conversation from the /rewind menu, Claude Code skips any tracked path that is a symlink or hard link and shows a Restored the code, but skipped N files warning. The skipped files keep their current contents." Examples given: "Config files a dotfile manager symlinks into your project and files pnpm hard-links into place both fall into this category."
facts.limits: Only affects the two code-restore actions; skipped paths retain their pre-restore (current) contents and must be reverted manually or by asking Claude. Debug logging (/debug) before restoring writes skipped paths to ~/.claude/debug/<session-id>.txt.

facts.feature: Checkpointing is not a replacement for version control / relation to git
facts.behavior: "Checkpoints are designed for quick, session-level recovery. For permanent version history and collaboration, continue using version control, such as Git, for commits, branches, and long-term history."
facts.limits: Checkpointing is session-scoped and not a substitute for git commits/branches; the docs also point to git as the required fallback for restoring subagent edits that checkpointing cannot capture.

area: Claude Code's native plugin eval runner (`claude plugin eval` / `claude plugin eval init`): case format, grader types, run mechanics, ablation, thresholds, reports, and availability — plus Anthropic's general eval-authoring guidance and the separate skill-creator eval framework, as of 2026-09-28.

facts.behavior: "Each case is a directory under the plugin's eval directory that contains a prompt.md, a case.yaml, or both... anything inside a case directory, such as graders/ and fixture files, belongs to that case." Cases nest under a directory that is itself not a case, to group them.
facts.limits: Applies only under the plugin's eval directory (default evals/, or the configured alternative); results/ is written by runs and should be gitignored.

facts.behavior: "prompt.md frontmatter accepts these fields. An unknown key is an error." Fields: schema_version, name, description, tags, plugins, runs, expected_outcome, model, max_turns, timeout_seconds, allowed_tools, append_system_prompt, env.
facts.limits: runs: 1-50 (default 3); max_turns: cap 200 (default 10); timeout_seconds: cap 3600 (default 300); env keys must match EVAL_[A-Z0-9_]*, any other key fails the run; @path mentions in the body are not expanded into attachments.

facts.behavior: "case.yaml is an alternative or companion to prompt.md: it describes a case in YAML and adds the fields that point at other files... When both files exist, prompt.md frontmatter overrides the matching case.yaml fields, the prompt.md body is the prompt, and graders/*.md are added after any graders listed in case.yaml."
facts.limits: Requires schema_version "1.1" and name; context.scaffold_script/history_file/add_dirs and execution.prompt exist only in case.yaml, not in prompt.md.

facts.behavior: "A Bash script in the case directory that runs in the empty workspace before Claude starts, to create fixture files or a git repository. It runs only when you pass --scaffold... The script runs as you, outside the agent's sandbox."
facts.limits: Off by default; scoped to a single case directory; docs advise passing --scaffold "only for suites you or your organization wrote."

facts.behavior: "An earlier conversation to continue: save the transcript as a .jsonl file and name it in context.history_file, and the case's prompt becomes the next user turn."
facts.limits: Only inside case.yaml's context block; file must live in the case directory.

facts.behavior: "context.add_dirs: Directories inside the case directory that Claude may read during the run, granted read-only."
facts.limits: Directories must be inside the case directory; read-only only.

facts.feature: Six grader types, no custom code
facts.behavior: "Of the six types, regex, tool_used, tool_order, and file_exists are computed from the transcript and files and cost nothing, while llm and baseline call a judge model and add to the run's cost. There are no custom-code graders."
facts.limits: No mechanism exists for author-supplied scoring code; all grading is one of the six built-in types.

facts.behavior: "The JavaScript regex pattern is found in the target. Set match: not_contains to require absence or match: \"count:N\" to require exactly N matches. Put case-insensitivity in flags: i; inline (?i) isn't supported."
facts.limits: JavaScript regex syntax only; costs nothing (no judge-model call).

facts.behavior: "The number of calls to tool whose JSON-encoded input matches the optional input_match regex is between min, default 1, and max, default unlimited. To assert a tool was never called, set both min: 0 and max: 0."
facts.limits: Matches on JSON-encoded tool input via regex only.

facts.behavior: "Both tools were called and the first matching before call precedes the first matching after call. Each is a tool name or { tool, input_match }."
facts.limits: Checks only first-matching-call ordering of two named tools.

facts.behavior: "A file Claude created matches the path glob, or none does with exists: false. Only files created during the run count."
facts.limits: "file_exists counts only files created during the run, so a file the scaffold created or that Claude only edited is invisible to it; grade its contents, or use tool_used on Edit."

facts.behavior: "A judge model votes PASS on the rubric in at least two of three votes. In the .md layout the file body is the criteria."
facts.limits: Judge model is "a small fast model" by default (overridable with --judge-model); costs a model call.

facts.behavior: "A judge finds the run satisfies the criteria at least as well as the reference transcript at baseline_file, a .jsonl in the case directory."
facts.limits: Requires an author-supplied reference transcript file in the case directory.

facts.behavior: regex graders take target, llm graders take focus, same value set: last_message (default, "Claude's final response text"); trace ("regex grader sees every message; an llm judge sees the first 12 and the last 12", JSON-escaped); files ("the list of paths Claude created during the run, one per line. Not their contents"); { source: file, path } ("contents of one file in the workspace after the run"; images shown to llm judge, other binaries refused); mock_calls ("each call Claude made to a mocked MCP tool, with its input and the mock's answer").
facts.limits: trace regex must match JSON-escaped text (e.g. \" not "); llm judge on trace only sees first/last 12 messages, not the full transcript; llm judge refuses non-image binary files (e.g. .pptx, PDF).

facts.behavior: "weight: Relative weight in the run's score. Any positive number" (default 1).
facts.limits: Applies per-grader within one case; affects the fraction-passed score computation.

facts.behavior: "arm: with-only excludes the grader from scoring in a two-arm run; both forces a grader Claude Code would otherwise exclude to be scored in both arms."
facts.limits: Only meaningful under the default two-arm (with-without) ablation mode.

facts.behavior: "A run's score is the fraction of its graders that passed, weighted if you set weights, and the case's score is the mean across its runs. A case passes when its score meets the --threshold, 1.0 by default."
facts.limits: Scoring is per-case, based on with-arm score only for pass/fail purposes.

facts.feature: Default runs per case (repetition for non-determinism)
facts.behavior: "One run of a non-deterministic agent tells you little, so each case runs three times by default."
facts.limits: Default 3, overridable 1-50 via runs frontmatter or via --runs (CLI); applies per arm.

facts.behavior: "For each run of a case, Claude Code starts a fresh, isolated, non-interactive session with only your plugin loaded, sends the prompt, and lets Claude work until it finishes or hits the case's turn or time limit."
facts.limits: Runs as a `claude -p` child process; only the target plugin is loaded, nothing else.

facts.feature: Isolation scope (what a run cannot see/use)
facts.behavior: "Nothing personal or project-level loads. Your user settings, hooks, CLAUDE.md files, MCP servers, other installed plugins, memory, and skills are absent, and no project-scoped .claude/ or .mcp.json above the sandbox is read... The Artifact tool is off... The case definitions are hidden from the agent... No network sandbox outside shell commands."
facts.limits: Managed-settings policy on the machine still applies inside a run ("results on a managed machine can differ from an unmanaged one by that policy"); a skill that publishes an artifact can only be graded on what it produces before that step.

facts.behavior: "Run up to this many agent runs at once (1-8; default 1). Each run is a full claude child on your own credential, so they share one rate limit; results and the report keep case order."
facts.limits: Capped at 8; shortens wall-clock time only, does not raise throughput past the account rate limit.

facts.behavior: "Each case's runs are repeated with no plugin loaded by default, and you get two scores, WITH and W/OUT. Their difference, Δ, is what the plugin contributed."
facts.limits: Default is with-without "whenever a plugin resolves" and none when no plugin resolves; roughly doubles agent-run cost when active.

facts.behavior: Excluded from score, reported as pass/fail indicators only in the with-arm: "Every tool_used grader whose tool is Skill"; "Every regex grader with target: mock_calls and every llm grader with focus: mock_calls, when each mocked server in the case is one your plugin declares"; "Any grader you mark arm: with-only."
facts.limits: "if every grader in a case is in the excluded set, they're scored normally instead"; overridable per-grader with arm: both; disabled entirely under --ablation none.

facts.behavior: "Pass --ablation none to run only the with-arm, which halves the cost when you don't need the comparison, such as while iterating on graders."
facts.limits: Report/summary shows SCORE and PASS% instead of WITH/W-OUT/Δ; under this mode "nothing is excluded, so the same suite can produce a different absolute score in the two modes."

facts.behavior: "A case passes when its with-arm score is at least this. Any case below it makes the command exit 1." Default 1.0.
facts.limits: Gates only the exit code, not the report content; the with-minus-without Δ never affects the exit code.

facts.behavior: "A ceiling on the run's list-price cost estimate, not on plan usage. Checked before each run starts. Once spent, nothing further starts; runs that already started finish, so spend can pass the ceiling by those runs. If any run is left unstarted, the command exits 2 with partial results."
facts.limits: Per --help: "the ceiling is checked before each run launches, so overrun is bounded to the runs in flight (one, or up to --concurrency)... when a run breaches, paid graders (llm/baseline) are skipped while free graders still score it." No ceiling by default.

facts.behavior: 0 = "Every case scored at or above --threshold and every case file loaded"; 1 = "A case scored below the threshold, a case file failed to load, no cases were found, a run couldn't be started, the plugin directory isn't trusted and --trust-plugin wasn't passed, or an option was invalid"; 2 = "Partial run: the --max-cost-usd ceiling was hit, or your credential was rejected before or at the first run"; 130 = "Interrupted"; 143 = "Terminated, such as by a CI timeout."
facts.limits: results.json is still written with partial: true and a reason on exit 2/130/143.

facts.behavior: "report.html is a single self-contained file that makes no external requests, so you can attach it to a CI job or open it from disk." Contains a verdict line, five summary tiles (suite score, ablation Δ, baseline score, cases passing threshold, perfect runs), per-case cards with Δ/score bar (red left edge if Δ negative), per-run grader pass/fail chips with explanations and (for llm graders) judge votes and evidence, and a Prompt/Graders section.
facts.limits: Written to <eval dir>/results/<timestamp>/report.html by default, or --report/--output-dir path.

facts.behavior: "If you're signed in with a claude.ai subscription and artifacts are available for your account, Claude Code also publishes the report as a private artifact and prints Published: <url>. Pass --no-publish to keep it local. If no Published: line appears, such as with API-key authentication, the local file is the report." "A run that a Claude Code session started... also stays local, and its Report: line says kept local. Add --publish-report to that command to publish it."
facts.limits: Publishing availability is gated on claude.ai subscription + artifacts eligibility; never publishes under API-key auth; session-initiated runs default to local-only.

facts.behavior: "aggregate-result.json, and --json output, is a versioned document with schemaVersion: 1 for CI scripts to parse. Field names are camelCase and new fields are added without renaming existing ones." Key fields: partial/partialReason, aggregates.overallScore, aggregates.casesPassed/casesTotal, aggregates.meanDelta, cases[].aggregates.score/delta, cases[].arms.with[].error/aborted/skippedPaidGraders, costUsd, durationSeconds, claudeVersion.
facts.limits: "Leave partial results out of trend charts"; "cases[].aggregates.delta ... Omitted when the arms aren't comparable"; costUsd is a list-price estimate, not actual billing.

facts.behavior: "A run never starts your plugin's real MCP servers unless you ask. Claude Code registers a substitute server under each server's own name. Tools with a mock file answer from it and are allowed without an --allow-tools grant, and a tool with no mock file isn't available to Claude."
facts.limits: Applies only to MCP servers declared in the plugin's own MCP configuration; a server with no mocks shows as "[not started: no mock]" in progress output.

facts.behavior: "--allow-real-servers: start the real process for each server you haven't mocked, and keep answering mocked tools from their files." "--mocks off: ignore mocks/ entirely and start every server the plugin declares."
facts.limits: "those processes run as you, outside the run's sandbox, and their tools need an --allow-tools grant" (e.g. mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__*).

facts.behavior: "the expect: block guards the input. If a call violates it, the run aborts with score 0 and records why, so a case can assert what your plugin asked the server to do."
facts.limits: Guard is per mocked tool file; violation is recorded in cases[].arms.with[].aborted with server, tool, and reason.

facts.behavior: "A type: agent mock answers with a call to the --judge-model, so its output varies between runs and changes if you change the judge. When a run completes without an error or abort, Claude Code saves each answer an agent mock gave under the results directory in mock-recordings/." Copying a recording into .replay/<server>/ makes "later runs answer the identical call from it with no model call."
facts.limits: Replay only applies once a recording is manually copied into .replay/; docs advise committing mocks/.replay/ "so CI runs are repeatable."

facts.feature: Tool grants (--allow-tools) and default read-only set
facts.behavior: "A run allows only the read-only tools the case lists in allowed_tools, from Read, Glob, Grep, NotebookRead, Skill, AskUserQuestion, Agent, TodoWrite, and the task tools TaskCreate, TaskGet, TaskList, TaskUpdate, and TaskStop, plus whatever you grant with --allow-tools... Built-in tools that need a grant you didn't give, such as Bash, Write, Edit, WebFetch, and WebSearch, are removed from the session, so Claude can't call them at all."
facts.limits: The --allow-tools grant applies to every case in the whole run, not per-case; a case's allowed_tools or a skill's own allowed-tools frontmatter "can't widen" this gate.

facts.behavior: "When you grant Bash in any form, every command runs under Claude Code's OS-level sandbox. Writes are confined to the run's workspace, your home directory and Claude Code configuration are unreadable, and network access is limited to domains you grant with --allow-tools \"WebFetch(domain:example.com)\". If you grant Bash or PowerShell on a machine with no sandbox backend, Claude Code refuses each run rather than running it unconfined."
facts.limits: "Native Windows has no backend, so run shell-granting suites under WSL2; on Linux, install bubblewrap and socat first."

facts.feature: Trust prompt for the plugin directory
facts.behavior: "The first time you run claude plugin eval against a directory, Claude Code asks 'Trust this plugin directory?' before it loads anything from it... When stdin or stdout isn't a terminal, under --json, or when the CI environment variable is set to a true value such as true, the run can't ask and is refused with exit 1; pass --trust-plugin to assert the trust yourself, only for a plugin you'd run on your own machine."
facts.limits: "A target you name rather than give as a path, meaning an installed plugin or a skills-directory plugin, skips the prompt." Inside a git repo, accepting trusts the whole repository.

facts.behavior: "Git 2.31 or later, if git is installed. With an older git, claude plugin eval stops before running any case. Without git, it runs normally." Error text: "git 2.30 is too old for claude plugin eval: it ignores the environment configuration (GIT_CONFIG_COUNT, added in git 2.31) that switches off the repository's git hooks and helper programs for the run."
facts.limits: "Before v2.1.283, claude plugin eval didn't check the git version, and on an older git the suite ran with those programs left on" — version-dependent behavior.

facts.behavior: "Claude Code v2.1.269 or later. Run claude --version to check and claude update to upgrade."
facts.limits: Older builds show "plugin eval is currently in early access."

facts.behavior: "'plugin eval is currently unavailable': Anthropic has switched the command off server-side. Nothing on your machine turns it back on; run claude update and try again in a fresh session later."
facts.limits: Not user-controllable; account/server-side gate independent of local Claude Code version once past early access.

facts.feature: claude plugin eval init authoring interview
facts.behavior: "claude plugin eval init asks you about your plugin, proposes the cases and graders, tries them, and writes the files." "Use --bare <name> for a blank single-case template." "-i, --interactive: Run the authoring interview (already the default in a terminal); requires an interactive terminal."
facts.limits: "init in CI: claude plugin eval init needs a terminal to ask you its questions; in CI, run claude plugin eval init --bare <name> to get the blank template."

facts.behavior: "experimental.evals: Path, or array of paths. Directory that holds the plugin's eval cases when it isn't the default evals/. claude plugin eval --eval-dir overrides it." "An unusable manifest value prints a Warning: line and the run uses evals/ instead."
facts.limits: Must be a relative path of plain directory names (e.g. qa, quality/evals); no absolute path or path containing `..`.

facts.behavior: "Give a relative path of plain directory names such as qa or quality/evals. An absolute path or one containing .. isn't accepted: as a flag value it's an error." If both the flag and the manifest set a directory, "the flag's directory is used."
facts.limits: Applies to both claude plugin eval and claude plugin eval init.

facts.behavior: Target is "a path, a plugin name, or a plugin@marketplace id — installed and skills-dir plugins both resolve (and add a no-plugin baseline arm)." Table: plugin root dir runs every case; a single prompt.md/case.yaml runs that case; an installed plugin by name/name@marketplace runs "the cases in the installed copy's eval directory, with the installed copy loaded," results under ./evals/results/ in the current directory; name@skills-dir is the same for a skills-directory plugin; omitted defaults to the current directory as a path.
facts.limits: Results location differs by target type (under the plugin vs. under the current working directory).

facts.behavior: "The judge for llm and baseline graders is a small fast model by default. Pass --judge-model sonnet or a full model ID to use a stronger one for nuanced rubrics."
facts.limits: Only affects llm and baseline graders, not the agent-under-test model.

facts.feature: --model pin for the agent under test
facts.behavior: Default: "Each case's model, else ANTHROPIC_MODEL if set, else Claude Code's default." Docs advise: "Pin it in CI so a model rollout isn't mistaken for a plugin regression."
facts.limits: Per-run override applies to the with-arm and without-arm agent, not the judge model.

facts.behavior: "The isolation described in this section limits what the agent under test can reach; it isn't a boundary against the plugin's own code, and a suite that passes says nothing about whether the plugin is safe." "When the plugin includes hooks you didn't write, or you start its real MCP servers, treat its scores as advisory unless you ran it in an isolated environment such as a container or CI runner, since hooks and servers run outside the agent's sandbox and could modify the files the graders read."
facts.limits: Applies specifically when a plugin has unreviewed hooks or real (non-mocked) MCP servers are started.

facts.behavior: "For iterating on one skill inside a Claude Code conversation, the skill-creator plugin runs a similar comparison with its own evals/evals.json format, and neither tool reads the other's case files."
facts.limits: `claude plugin eval` (plugin-level, prompt.md/case.yaml/graders) and skill-creator's evals.json (skill-level) are two distinct, non-interoperable systems.

facts.behavior: Recommends a task-based approach with defined components: Tasks (individual tests with defined inputs and success criteria), Trials (multiple runs per task to handle model non-determinism), Graders (logic scoring performance aspects), Transcripts (complete records of interactions and tool calls), and Outcomes (final environmental state, not just stated completion).
facts.limits: General engineering guidance for building custom agent evals; not a description of, or requirement enforced by, the `claude plugin eval` tool itself.

facts.behavior: Code-based graders: "Fast, Cheap, Objective, Reproducible, Easy to debug" for unit tests/static analysis/outcome checks, but brittle to valid variations. Model-based graders: "Flexible, Scalable, Captures nuance, Handles open-ended tasks," requiring calibration against human judgment to avoid hallucinated verdicts. Human graders: "Gold standard quality, Matches expert user judgment," used to calibrate LLM judges and grade subjective outputs.
facts.limits: General guidance, independent of `claude plugin eval`'s six specific grader types.

facts.feature: Anthropic guidance: grade outcomes, not the path taken
facts.behavior: "Grade what the agent produced, not the path it took," to avoid penalizing creative valid solutions; recommends balanced datasets with both positive and negative cases to prevent one-sided optimization.
facts.limits: A design recommendation for authoring graders, not a rule the runner enforces.

facts.feature: Anthropic guidance: pass@k / pass^k for non-determinism
facts.behavior: "Use pass@k (likelihood of ≥1 success in k attempts) and pass^k (probability all k trials succeed) metrics depending on product requirements." Also: "You won't know if your graders are working well unless you read the transcripts and grades from many trials."
facts.limits: Metric choice depends on the product's tolerance for failure; general guidance not tied to a specific tool's implementation.

facts.behavior: "Start with 20-50 realistic tasks from actual failures rather than waiting for hundreds. Create reference solutions proving solvability, maintain isolated environments between trials, and continuously monitor for eval saturation to ensure continued signal for improvement."
facts.limits: Sizing/process guidance, not an enforced minimum or maximum case count in any tool.

facts.behavior: "If you've written software tests, this will feel familiar: define some test prompts (plus files if needed), describe what good looks like, and skill-creator tells you whether the skill holds up."
facts.limits: Describes skill-creator's own authoring flow for its evals/evals.json format, not `claude plugin eval`.

facts.behavior: Supports "A/B testing through comparator agents that evaluate two versions side-by-side—'skill vs. no skill' or competing skill implementations... They judge outputs without knowing which is which, so you can tell whether a change actually helped."
facts.limits: Skill-level, blind-comparison ablation distinct from `claude plugin eval`'s named with/without-plugin arms (which are not blind to the judge).

facts.behavior: "Benchmark mode runs standardized assessments tracking three metrics: Eval pass rate, Elapsed time, Token usage. This enables teams to detect regressions when models update or during iterative skill refinement."
facts.limits: skill-creator-specific feature; distinct metric set from `claude plugin eval`'s cost/score/Δ reporting.

area: Claude Code native support for: skills, slash commands, disable-model-invocation, skill frontmatter, skill-doctor, plugin init scaffolding (as of 2026-09-28, Claude Code v2.1.283)

facts.behavior: "Create a SKILL.md file with instructions, and Claude adds it to its toolkit. Claude uses skills when relevant, or you can invoke one directly with /skill-name."
facts.limits: All frontmatter fields are optional; the skill's body loads into context only when invoked (manually or by Claude), not kept resident like CLAUDE.md.

facts.behavior: Skills load from Enterprise (.claude/skills in managed settings dir), Personal (~/.claude/skills), Project (.claude/skills), Nested (<subdir>/.claude/skills), --add-dir directories, Plugin (<plugin>/skills), and claude.ai account (synced). "Skills in a .claude/skills/ directory below where you started don't load at startup. They load the first time Claude reads or edits a file in that subdirectory." Precedence: enterprise over personal, personal over project.
facts.limits: Personal skills load in all projects on this machine but NOT in Cowork or cloud sessions. Reserved folder names 'synced' and 'anthropic-skills' are skipped if authored locally.

facts.behavior: "Set to true to prevent Claude from automatically loading this skill. Use for workflows you want to trigger manually with /name. Also prevents the skill from being preloaded into subagents. As of v2.1.196, also prevents the skill from running when a scheduled task fires with the skill as its prompt." Truth table: you-can-invoke=Yes, Claude-can-invoke=No, and "description not in context, full skill loads when you invoke."
facts.limits: Default is false. Does not restrict manual invocation via /name or the skillOverrides menu; only blocks Claude's own automatic/model-initiated invocation and subagent preloading and scheduled-task firing.

facts.behavior: "Set to false when only Claude should invoke the skill: Claude Code hides it from the / menu and doesn't run it when you type /name. Use for background knowledge users shouldn't invoke directly."
facts.limits: Default is true. Inverse of disable-model-invocation: Claude can still invoke it automatically; only the human-typed /name path is blocked.

facts.behavior: "Tools Claude can use without asking permission during the turn that invokes this skill. The grant clears when you send your next message... It does not restrict which tools are available: every tool remains callable, and your permission settings still govern tools that are not listed." "Workspace trust doesn't gate this field. Claude Code applies a project skill's allowed-tools whenever you or Claude invoke the skill, including in a -p run in a folder you've never trusted."
facts.limits: Grant is scoped to the single turn that invoked the skill; re-invoking re-applies it. Supports bash rules and path substitutions like ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}. A repo-checked-in skill can grant itself broad tool access without a trust prompt.

facts.behavior: "Tools removed from Claude's available pool while this skill is active. Use for autonomous skills that should never call certain tools... Like deny rules, the field can't remove EndConversation while any other tool remains."
facts.limits: Restriction clears when the next message is sent (same turn-scoping as allowed-tools).

facts.behavior: "Glob patterns that limit when this skill is activated... When set, Claude loads the skill automatically only when working with files matching the patterns. Uses the same format as path-specific rules."
facts.limits: Not available on legacy command files: "A command file in .claude/commands/ accepts the same fields except name and paths." Governs automatic loading only, not manual /name invocation.

facts.behavior: model: "Model to use when this skill is active. The override applies for the rest of the current turn and isn't saved to settings... Values excluded by org's availableModels allowlist aren't used." effort: "Effort level when this skill is active. Overrides the session effort level. Options: low, medium, high, xhigh, max; available levels depend on the model."
facts.limits: Turn-scoped only; session model/effort resumes on the next prompt. With context: fork, model instead sets the forked subagent's model.

facts.behavior: "Add context: fork to your frontmatter when you want a skill to run in isolation. Claude Code starts a new subagent of the type set in the agent field and gives it the skill content as its prompt. The subagent doesn't see your conversation history." "The forked subagent runs in the background... Set background: false ... to instead wait for the result in the turn that invoked the skill." "A forked skill that runs in the background applies its edits outside your session's checkpoints, so /rewind doesn't undo them; use git to revert them."
facts.limits: background:false requires v2.1.218+. Claude Code still waits synchronously in non-interactive (-p) mode, when CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1, when an earlier invocation of the same forked skill is still running, or when a scheduled task fires it. A backgrounded fork runs with the narrower background-subagent tool set.

facts.feature: hooks / metadata / license / compatibility frontmatter fields
facts.behavior: hooks: "Hooks that Claude Code registers when the skill is invoked and keeps running for the rest of the session." metadata: "Free-form YAML map for your own key-value data... Claude Code doesn't act on its contents, and drops a value that isn't a map." license and compatibility: "Part of the Agent Skills spec; Claude Code accepts the field but doesn't act on it."
facts.limits: compatibility is capped at 500 characters. license/compatibility/metadata are no-ops inside Claude Code itself (relevant only to the external Agent Skills spec/claude.ai upload).

facts.behavior: "Boolean fields accept yes, no, on, off, 1, and 0 in any letter case, in addition to true and false. Before v2.1.218, Claude Code recognized only true and false."
facts.limits: Version-gated: pre-v2.1.218 only true/false worked.

facts.behavior: "Claude Code reads the frontmatter only when the opening --- is the file's first line. Otherwise it treats the whole file, --- markers included, as skill content." "If the YAML between the markers doesn't parse, the skill still loads with no fields set."
facts.limits: Fails open rather than blocking: a broken or missing frontmatter block never prevents the skill from loading, it just loses field-level configuration (or the whole file becomes body text).

facts.feature: Custom slash commands merged into skills
facts.behavior: "Custom commands have been merged into skills. A file at .claude/commands/deploy.md and a skill at .claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md both create /deploy and work the same way." "Your existing .claude/commands/ files keep working. Skills add optional features: a directory for supporting files, frontmatter to control whether you or Claude invokes them, and the ability for Claude to load them automatically when relevant."
facts.limits: Legacy .claude/commands/<name>.md files lack name/paths frontmatter support and the supporting-files directory that skill folders get.

facts.behavior: Precedence order: enterprise over personal/project skills; "custom skills replace bundled skills (but not aliases)"; skills over .claude/commands/ files; a project-root skill and a same-named nested skill both stay available (root runs on bare /name, nested reachable as /dir:name); plugin skills namespaced as /plugin-name:skill-name; synced-skill name collisions run the other command under the short name while the synced one is reachable only as /anthropic-skills:<name>.
facts.limits: Plugin name-prefix doubling bug existed v2.1.216–v2.1.245 (fixed v2.1.246+) when a skill's own name field already carried the plugin prefix.

facts.behavior: "Typing /write-tests /fix-issue 123 loads both skills and passes the trailing text 123 as $ARGUMENTS to each of them." "Claude Code expands the first skill plus up to five more stacked after it."
facts.limits: Hard cap of 6 skills expanded per message (1 + 5). Before v2.1.199, only the first skill loaded and received the rest as literal argument text.

facts.behavior: "Indexed arguments use shell-style quoting... The $ARGUMENTS placeholder always expands to the full argument string as typed." "An indexed placeholder with no corresponding argument... stays in the content unchanged. A named placeholder from the arguments frontmatter with no matching argument expands to an empty string." "If you invoke a skill with arguments but no placeholder in the skill's content receives one, Claude Code appends ARGUMENTS: <your input> to the end of the skill content." Escaping: "escape it with a backslash: \$1.00. A backslash before any other $ is left unchanged."
facts.limits: arguments frontmatter maps names to positions in declaration order only.

facts.behavior: "Claude Code runs shell commands before the skill content is sent to Claude. The command output replaces the placeholder, so Claude receives actual data, not the command itself." "A failed command aborts the entire skill invocation, not just its own placeholder. Claude never sees the skill content for that invocation." "Injected commands never prompt for permission while the skill renders. Claude Code checks each one against your permission rules first. A command a deny rule matches aborts the invocation." Toggle: set "disableSkillShellExecution": true in settings to replace each command with "[shell command execution disabled by policy]" for user/project/plugin/additional-directory skills ("Bundled and managed skills are not affected").
facts.limits: Each command runs under the Bash tool's default 2-minute timeout, in the session's current cwd. "Claude Code doesn't run these commands on your machine when the skill is synced from your claude.ai account" (requires v2.1.228+). Non-zero exit fails the whole render, except exit code 1 from search/comparison commands is treated as normal output.

facts.feature: Skill content lifecycle and auto-compaction budget
facts.behavior: "When you or Claude invoke a skill, the rendered SKILL.md content enters the conversation as a single message and stays there across later turns... Claude Code does not re-read the skill file on later turns." "When Claude re-invokes a skill whose rendered content is identical to the copy already in context, Claude Code adds a short note that the skill is already loaded rather than a second copy." "Auto-compaction... re-attaches the most recent invocation of each skill after the summary, keeping the first 5,000 tokens of each. Re-attached skills share a combined budget of 25,000 tokens."
facts.limits: 5,000-token cap per re-attached skill after compaction; 25,000-token combined cap across all re-attached skills.

facts.behavior: Four states per skill name: "on" (name+description listed, in / menu), "name-only" (name only listed, in / menu), "user-invocable-only" (hidden from Claude's listing, still in / menu), "off" (hidden entirely). "A skill that is absent from skillOverrides is treated as on." "The /skills menu writes it for you: highlight a skill and press Space to cycle states, then Esc to save to .claude/settings.local.json." "Invoking a hidden skill by its full name still returns the skillOverrides error instead of running it."
facts.limits: As of v2.1.199, "off" also hides the skill from Remote Control clients and Agent SDK callers, not just the terminal / menu.

facts.behavior: "Permission syntax: Skill(name) for exact match, Skill(name *) for prefix match with any arguments." "If your deny rule names an alias or an unqualified name rather than the skill's own name, Claude Code still blocks the skill... Claude Code matches an allow rule only against the skill's own name and the name in Claude's invocation." A bare Skill rule with no args disables all skills.
facts.limits: "In an allow rule, a prefix outside the namespace reserved for synced skills doesn't match the names inside it: Skill(anthropic *) doesn't cover anthropic-skills:pdf." Nested-skill qualified-name deny matching fixed only from v2.1.260+.

facts.behavior: "Claude Code watches skill directories for file changes, except in bare mode. When you add, edit, or remove a skill under ~/.claude/skills/, the project .claude/skills/, or a .claude/skills/ inside an --add-dir directory, Claude Code picks up the change within the current session, without a restart." "Live change detection covers SKILL.md text only. For a skill folder that is also a plugin, changes to hooks/, .mcp.json, agents/, and output-styles/ need /reload-plugins to take effect."
facts.limits: A brand-new top-level skills directory (didn't exist at session start) requires manual /reload-skills, and again after each subsequent change to it.

facts.behavior: "Claude Code includes a set of bundled skills, such as /doctor, /code-review, /batch, /debug, /loop, and /claude-api. Bundled skills are prompt-based: they give Claude detailed instructions and let it orchestrate the work using its tools." "To turn bundled skills off, use the disableBundledSkills setting." Individual bundled skills can also be hidden via skillOverrides "off".
facts.limits: The documented bundled-skill list does NOT include anything named 'skill-doctor'. "Most bundled skills are available in every session. A few depend on a specific feature."

facts.behavior: "In your terminal, Claude Code syncs those skills in sessions where you sign in with your claude.ai account. area: Claude Code native support for settings precedence and merge chain, managed settings, model allow/deny lists, auto mode configuration, and enterprise lockout (as of 2026-09-28)

facts.behavior: "When the same key appears in more than one place, Claude Code uses the value from the highest level that sets it." Order, highest first: 1) Managed settings (managed-settings.json, MDM, or the claude.ai console) — "Nothing you set overrides them"; 2) Command line (`claude --settings`), applies above user/project/local, below managed, lasts one session; 3) Project local settings (.claude/settings.local.json); 4) Shared project settings (.claude/settings.json); 5) User settings (~/.claude/settings.json).
facts.limits: Environment variables are not a level in this stack; each variable/key pair is resolved individually (e.g. ANTHROPIC_MODEL overrides `model` from any file, ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL only applies when no file sets `model`). An `env` block inside a settings file is an ordinary key and follows the 5-level stack.

facts.feature: List settings merge across files instead of overriding
facts.behavior: "When you set the same list key, such as permissions.allow, in more than one file, Claude Code combines the lists instead of picking one, so each file can add entries without removing another file's."
facts.limits: Four model-related keys do NOT merge: fallbackModel (whole chain taken from highest-precedence file), modelPicker (whole value, taken only from managed/--settings/user, ignored in project and local settings, requires v2.1.242+), availableModels (when managed settings define it, that list is applied as-is and entries added in user/project/local are ignored; merges normally across non-managed scopes), modelSettings (resolved per-model together with effortLevel).

facts.feature: Exceptions to managed settings precedence (stricter lower-level value wins)
facts.behavior: "For a few keys whose values restrict a session, Claude Code honors a restrictive value from a scope that otherwise couldn't override managed settings." Table: disableClaudeAiConnectors (true from any scope, honored even if managed sets false); enableArtifact (false from any scope, or disableArtifact:true, honored even if managed sets true, nothing turns it back on); isolatePeerMachines (true from any scope); remoteControlAtStartup (false from project/local settings, honored even if managed sets true); crossSessionInbound (stricter value from project/local on accept<hold<refuse ladder); useAutoModeDuringPlan (false from any managed source, --settings, user, or local); syncClaudeAiSkills (false, same scopes); syncClaudeAiPlugins (false, same scopes); maxEffortLevel (lower cap from any scope, including --settings, wins; requires v2.1.267+).
facts.limits: Applies only to these named security-sensitive keys; every other key is fully overridden by managed settings with no exception.

facts.behavior: "An app that runs Claude Code inside itself and sets CLAUDE_CODE_PROVIDER_MANAGED_BY_HOST is also an exception. Claude Code takes that app's model configuration over the model, fallbackModel, modelPicker, and modelOverrides keys from every managed source, and over the model-selection variables in a managed env block... Claude Code keeps a managed availableModels allowlist in force unless the app supplies its own."
facts.limits: Only applies when the embedding host sets this specific environment variable; the managed availableModels allowlist still applies unless the host supplies its own.

facts.behavior: A cloud session "runs in a cloud environment on a fresh clone of your repository, not on your machine." Shared project settings (.claude/settings.json) are read for a single-repo session (multi-repo sessions read only `enabledPlugins` and `extraKnownMarketplaces` from each repo's file, not permission rules/hooks/env). "User and project local settings... not read. Both stay on your machine." "Managed settings: only server-managed settings reach a cloud session; a managed-settings.json file or MDM profile on your device doesn't." A self-hosted environment also reads the managed settings file in its runner image.
facts.limits: Applies specifically to claude.ai/code cloud sessions and self-hosted environments; does not describe local terminal/IDE/desktop sessions.

facts.feature: Managed settings file (top of precedence, per-OS location)
facts.behavior: "Managed settings are the settings your organization deploys to every developer's machine. Claude Code applies them above every other level, so no user, project, local, or --settings value overrides them, apart from a few security-sensitive exceptions." File paths: macOS `/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/managed-settings.json`; Linux and WSL `/etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json`; Windows `C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\managed-settings.json`.
facts.limits: "Claude Code doesn't read the legacy Windows path C:\ProgramData\ClaudeCode\managed-settings.json." File-based delivery is one of four mechanisms (also server-managed/console, MDM/OS policy, HKCU registry).

facts.feature: managed-settings.d/ drop-in directory (split policy across teams)
facts.behavior: "Claude Code merges managed-settings.json first, then every *.json file in the directory in alphabetical order." Merge rules when two files set the same key: single values — later file's value replaces earlier; lists (e.g. permissions.deny, sandbox.network.allowedDomains) — combine with duplicates removed; nested blocks (env, sandbox) — merge key by key; fallbackModel — later chain replaces whole; extraKnownMarketplaces and managedMcpServers — later entry with same name replaces whole; modelPicker — later lineup replaces whole.
facts.limits: Claude Code ignores hidden files and files that don't end in .json. Located next to managed-settings.json in the same system directory.

facts.behavior: Default `"first-wins"`: "Claude Code uses the highest-ranked source that delivers at least one policy key and ignores the rest rather than merging them." `"merge"` (requires v2.1.242+): "Claude Code applies every admin source that delivers a policy key and combines them by kind of key: on most keys the higher-ranked source's value applies, lists union, and locks take the strictest value." Source rank, highest first: 1) Remote/server-managed settings (claude.ai console or Claude apps gateway), 2) MDM or OS-level policy, 3) managed-settings files (managed-settings.json + managed-settings.d/*.json merged), 4) HKCU registry (Windows/WSL only, user-writable, read only when no higher source delivers a policy key, never merges).
facts.limits: Managed-only key: "Claude Code reads the key only from the highest-ranked source that carries either the key or a policy key, so a lower source can't opt itself into merging." HKCU registry never counts as an "admin source" for merge purposes.

facts.feature: Cross-source keys (read from every admin source under first-wins)
facts.behavior: "Claude Code reads them from every admin source, so a lower-ranked MDM policy or managed settings file can still set them when the selected source doesn't." Includes: sandbox.network.allowManagedDomainsOnly and sandbox.filesystem.allowManagedReadPathsOnly (a true in any admin source turns the lock on; allowlists union across sources while locked), allowAllClaudeAiMcps, allowManagedMcpServersOnly, deniedMcpServers, disableClaudeAiConnectors, sandbox.bwrapPath/socatPath/ripgrep, sandbox.filesystem.disabled, sandbox.network.strictAllowlist, useAutoModeDuringPlan/syncClaudeAiSkills/syncClaudeAiPlugins (false from any admin source turns behavior off), enableArtifact (false from any admin source turns it off; nothing turns it back on), maxEffortLevel (lowest cap from any admin source applies), a commit-trailer opt-out in `attribution`, forceRemoteSettingsRefresh, and `env` (merged per-variable, highest-priority source per variable wins).
facts.limits: HKCU registry excluded from this scan except when it is the only source present.

facts.feature: policyHelper — compute managed settings via executable
facts.behavior: "A policyHelper is an executable your MDM policy or managed settings file names, and Claude Code runs it to compute managed settings at startup. When the selected source configures one and the helper emits a managedSettings object... The emitted managedSettings object is the only managed settings for the session," including for cross-source keys (except forceRemoteSettingsRefresh).
facts.limits: Managed-only key. A new/changed policyHelper entry takes effect at next launch. "Any schema violation that survives fails the whole helper run, and at startup Claude Code refuses to start," same as a helper that exits non-zero.

facts.feature: parentSettingsBehavior — policy from an embedding host (e.g. Claude Desktop, IDE extension, Agent SDK app)
facts.behavior: "By default, Claude Code ignores parent settings whenever an admin source is present." Set to `"merge"` in the highest-priority managed source to have Claude Code "merge parent settings alongside an admin source... Claude Code then keeps only the host's values that restrict what Claude can do."
facts.limits: Gap noted: "unless you also set the allowManaged*Only locks, the host's permission allow rules and sandbox allowlists still apply" regardless of this setting. Managed-only key, read only from the highest-priority source. A policyHelper can override this key.

facts.feature: What a developer can change despite managed settings
facts.behavior: "A developer's own settings files, --settings values, and project files never override a managed value... These cases sit outside that rule: The model for a session — a managed model is a default, not a lock. --model and ANTHROPIC_MODEL still pick the model for that session, so deploy availableModels to restrict the choice. Local admin rights — a developer who is an administrator on the machine can edit the managed source itself... The server-managed cache — an edit to the local cache lasts only until the next successful fetch. Other tools — managed settings bind Claude Code only. A developer who calls the API from another tool isn't under them."
facts.limits: Managed settings only govern the Claude Code binary/product; they have no effect on direct API usage outside it, and an OS-admin developer can edit the managed source file/registry itself.

facts.feature: Verifying a managed policy is in force (/status, claude doctor)
facts.behavior: "/status shows which managed source Claude Code selected, and claude doctor lists what it dropped." The Setting sources line shows a label in parentheses: (remote), (plist)/(HKLM), (file)/(drop-ins)/(file + drop-ins), "(remote + file, merged)" (or another list ending in ", merged"), (HKCU), (parent process), (helper). A missing line means "Claude Code found no managed source that delivers a policy key"; a line naming a different source than deployed means a higher-priority source is present and overrode it (shown in a `Skipped sources` line, v2.1.242+).
facts.limits: Diagnostic only; does not itself change enforcement.

facts.feature: Fail-closed handling of invalid managed settings entries
facts.behavior: "If your managed settings file, MDM profile, registry value, or server-managed payload fails schema validation, Claude Code first skips each individual entry it can repair... Claude Code then drops any value that still fails, unless the value belongs to one of the keys that fail closed instead." Examples: allowedMcpServers → enforced as empty allowlist until fixed; availableModels → enforced as empty allowlist so only the Default model is available; allowManagedHooksOnly / allowManagedMcpServersOnly / enforceAvailableModels / disableCommandPluginSources / disableSideloadFlags → treated as true until fixed; forceLoginOrgUUID → no organization permitted to log in until fixed; crossSessionInbound → treated as `refuse` (most restrictive) until fixed. requiredMinimumVersion and requiredMaximumVersion "fail open by design: an invalid value is dropped rather than enforced."
facts.limits: "This tolerance applies only to managed settings. User, project, and local settings files remain strict: a file whose JSON or top-level shape fails validation is rejected as a whole."

facts.feature: Keys only a managed source can set
facts.behavior: "Claude Code reads the following keys only from a managed source; placing them in user or project settings files has no effect." Named list includes allowAllClaudeAiMcps, allowedChannelPlugins, allowManagedHooksOnly, allowManagedMcpServersOnly, allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly, blockedMarketplaces, channelsEnabled, disableCommandPluginSources, disableSideloadFlags, forceRemoteSettingsRefresh, managedMcpServers, managedSourcesBehavior, parentSettingsBehavior, pluginSuggestionMarketplaces, pluginTrustMessage, policyHelper, sandbox.filesystem.allowManagedReadPathsOnly, sandbox.network.allowManagedDomainsOnly, strictKnownMarketplaces, strictPluginOnlyCustomization, wslInheritsWindowsSettings — plus (per the settings-reference Scope column) gateway login URL, version pinning, browser, mobile-simulator, SSH host, Desktop local-session, sandbox binary path, model pricing, model restriction, and CLAUDE.md controls.
facts.limits: "Most of them are locks: the value a lock governs... is an ordinary key that any level can set, and the lock tells Claude Code to honor only the managed value."

facts.behavior: "Make managed settings the only settings source of permission rules." Deploying it with a deny list "makes Claude Code ignore permission rules from user, project, and local files and from --allowedTools." It also causes Claude Code to drop parent-supplied (embedding-host) allow rules and additionalDirectories.
facts.limits: Managed-only key. In Cowork sessions this can strip pre-approved folder access the host would otherwise grant, requiring explicit managed allow rules to restore it.

facts.behavior: "When true, only allowedMcpServers from managed settings are respected. deniedMcpServers still merges from all sources." As a cross-source key, a true in any admin source turns the lock on, and "the managed allowedMcpServers list comes from the highest-ranked admin source that sets one" (requires v2.1.273+).
facts.limits: Managed-only key; fails closed as true when invalid.

facts.behavior: "sandbox.network.allowManagedDomainsOnly: Honor only managed allowedDomains and WebFetch(domain:...) allow rules; block other domains without prompting." "sandbox.filesystem.allowManagedReadPathsOnly: When true, only filesystem.allowRead paths from managed settings are respected. denyRead still merges from all sources."
facts.limits: Both are managed-only cross-source keys: a true in any admin source turns the lock on and the underlying allowlist unions across admin sources while locked.

facts.behavior: "Reject the --plugin-dir, --plugin-url, --agents, and --mcp-config flags at startup. In cloud sessions, Claude Code drops the MCP servers the server delivered through --mcp-config, other than in-process type: \"sdk\" entries, and starts the session."
facts.limits: Requires Claude Code v2.1.193 or later. Managed-only key; fails closed as true when invalid.

facts.behavior: "When true, blocks CLI startup until remote managed settings are freshly fetched and exits if the fetch fails."
facts.limits: Managed-only, cross-source key (read from every admin source); a change takes effect at the next session start.

facts.behavior: "Refuse to start on a version older than your organization requires" (requiredMinimumVersion) / "...newer than your organization allows" (requiredMaximumVersion). "requiredMinimumVersion blocks an outdated binary from starting and doesn't end a session that's already running" (long-lived sessions can lag a rollout). Changes to this key take effect at the next session start.
facts.limits: Managed-only. Fails OPEN by design: "an invalid value is dropped rather than enforced" (unlike most other managed keys, which fail closed).

facts.feature: Surface coverage of managed settings (where/when a policy reaches sessions)
facts.behavior: On the developer's machine: "the terminal, the VS Code and JetBrains extensions, the desktop app's Code tab, and Agent SDK sessions read all of these sources. Agent SDK sessions load managed settings even when settingSources excludes the user, project, and local files." Cloud sessions in an Anthropic-hosted environment "don't read a device's MDM profile or file, so policy for it has to come from server-managed settings." A self-hosted environment also reads the managed settings file in its runner image (by default only when server-managed settings deliver no policy key). Cowork sessions in Claude Desktop "never fetch server-managed settings from the claude.ai admin console"; on the user's machine they read device MDM/file policy by default, in a full VM sandbox (requireCoworkFullVmSandbox) device policy isn't present, and remote Cowork sessions run on Anthropic-managed VMs with no device policy at all.
facts.limits: Coverage differs meaningfully by surface; a policy deployed only as a device file/MDM profile will not reach a cloud or remote Cowork session.

facts.feature: Org-wide Remote Control / cloud sessions toggle (Team/Enterprise)
facts.behavior: "On Team and Enterprise plans, an Owner enables or disables Remote Control and cloud sessions organization-wide in Claude Code admin settings. Remote Control can additionally be disabled per device with the disableRemoteControl setting. Cloud sessions have no per-device managed settings key." "To check whether these organization settings reached a given machine, run claude doctor there and read the Organization policy line."
facts.limits: Cloud sessions can only be controlled at the organization/admin-console level, not via a per-device managed-settings.json key. Requires Claude Code v2.1.261+ for the doctor check.

facts.behavior: "Restrict which models people can pick." Settable from any settings file, but "when the managed settings Claude Code applies define it, Claude Code applies that list as-is and ignores entries you add in user, project, or local settings." A managed `model` sets only the session's starting default; "the lock is availableModels, which constrains /model, --model, and the model key in your own files."
facts.limits: Merges normally across non-managed scopes (user/project/local), but a managed-set list completely replaces rather than merges with lower scopes. If invalid, fails closed as an empty allowlist so only the Default model is available.

facts.behavior: "Make each availableModels model ID entry permit only the version it names" — blocks specific models or versions rather than whole model families.
facts.limits: Managed only. A "Lock" kind of key under managedSourcesBehavior=merge (strictest value across sources applies). Fails closed as `"exact"` when invalid.

facts.feature: enforceAvailableModels — enforce allowlist for the Default model choice
facts.behavior: "Keep the /model Default choice inside your availableModels allowlist."
facts.limits: Settable from any file. Fails closed as true when invalid.

facts.behavior: "Block specific models, even ones availableModels permits."
facts.limits: Managed only. A "Lists" kind of key under managedSourcesBehavior=merge (combines entries across sources). If invalid, a non-string entry is stripped and the rest enforced; a wholly invalid value is dropped with a warning and blocks no models until fixed.

facts.feature: Auto mode — permission classifier overview and availability
facts.behavior: "Auto mode lets Claude Code run without routine permission prompts by routing tool calls through a classifier that blocks anything irreversible, destructive, or aimed outside your environment. Deny and explicit ask rules are evaluated before the classifier and still block or prompt." "The classifier is a second gate that runs after the permissions system." "Auto mode is available to all users on every provider, including the Anthropic API, Claude Platform on AWS, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry, and signed-in Claude apps gateway sessions," and its availability is also gated by "the organization-level control on Team and Enterprise plans."
facts.limits: Only judges tool calls Claude is about to make; it doesn't replace the deny/ask permission layer that runs before it.

facts.feature: autoMode.environment — trusted infrastructure, and where autoMode config is read from
facts.behavior: "By default, the classifier trusts only the working directory and the current repo's configured remotes. Actions like pushing to your company's source-control org or writing to a team cloud bucket are blocked until you add them to autoMode.environment." The classifier reads autoMode from: one developer's `~/.claude/settings.json`, organization-wide managed settings, or the `--settings` flag / Agent SDK inline JSON (per-invocation). "The classifier doesn't read autoMode from project settings in .claude/settings.json or .claude/settings.local.json," specifically because either file could be committed to or injected by the repo itself.
facts.limits: "Entries from each scope are combined. A developer can extend environment, allow, soft_deny, and hard_deny with personal entries but can't remove entries that managed settings provide. Because allow rules act as exceptions to soft block rules inside the classifier, a developer-added allow entry can override an organization soft_deny entry: the combination is additive, not a hard policy boundary."

facts.feature: autoMode.hard_deny / soft_deny / allow — classifier rule tiers
facts.behavior: "hard_deny rules block unconditionally. User intent and allow exceptions don't apply." "soft_deny rules block next. User intent and allow exceptions can override these." "allow rules then override matching soft_deny rules as exceptions." "Explicit user intent overrides the remaining soft blocks: if the user's message directly and specifically describes the exact action Claude is about to take, the classifier allows it even when a soft_deny rule matches." Including the literal string "$defaults" keeps the built-in rules while splicing in custom ones; omitting it "replaces the entire default list for that section."
facts.limits: "General requests don't count as explicit intent. Asking Claude to 'clean up the repo' doesn't authorize force-pushing, but asking Claude to 'force-push this branch' does." For an unconditional boundary regardless of classifier config or user intent, docs say to use permissions.deny in managed settings instead, "which blocks the action before the classifier is consulted and can't be overridden."

facts.feature: autoMode.classifyAllShell — route every shell command through the classifier
facts.behavior: By default "narrow Bash and PowerShell allow rules such as Bash(npm test) stay in effect in auto mode... Claude Code suspends only the broad rules that grant arbitrary code execution, such as Bash(*) or wildcarded interpreters, together with every rule that names Monitor." Setting `autoMode.classifyAllShell: true` "suspend[s] every Bash and PowerShell allow rule while auto mode is active, so the classifier evaluates every shell command regardless of your allow list, except critical-path removals... trades latency for coverage."
facts.limits: "The setting applies only while auto mode is active, and your allow rules behave normally in other permission modes." Set from user or managed settings only (same scope restriction as autoMode).

facts.feature: permissions.ask / permissions.deny as checkpoints around the auto mode classifier
facts.behavior: "Content-scoped ask rules... are evaluated before the classifier and always force a permission prompt, even in auto mode, because an explicit ask rule is your stated intent to be prompted for that action." Table: permissions.ask — "Always prompts for a command that matches a content-scoped rule... The classifier cannot auto-approve a matching action." permissions.deny — "Blocks before the classifier is consulted. Neither the classifier nor user intent can override it."
facts.limits: "A push Claude writes another way, such as git -C <dir> push or git -c <key>=<value> push, doesn't match the rule, so it isn't checkpointed. For a checkpoint that inspects the full command text, add a PreToolUse hook."

facts.behavior: "Auto mode allows pushes to any branch of the repository you're working in, including the default branch, and pull request creation by default. A non-default branch whose name marks it as a deploy or publication target, such as production, release, or gh-pages, isn't covered by that default: the classifier judges a push there on its own terms... The push's content is also still checked, so a force push, a secret entering the commit, or a change that would send secrets outside the repository when CI or a deploy pipeline runs it stays blocked."
facts.limits: Default classifier behavior only; overridable via autoMode.soft_deny/hard_deny/allow or permissions.ask/deny.

facts.behavior: "Remove auto mode from the permission mode cycle."
facts.limits: Settable from any settings file per the settings-reference scope summary.

facts.behavior: "Skip the one-time notice Claude Code shows when you first enter auto mode yourself rather than through the built-in default."
facts.limits: User or managed scope.

facts.feature: permissions.defaultMode — default permission mode for new sessions (includes auto mode)
facts.behavior: "Set the permission mode new sessions start in." Values `auto` and `bypassPermissions` "don't take effect from project or local settings; set them in user or managed settings instead, or pass --permission-mode for one session. Before v2.1.257, bypassPermissions took effect from any file."
facts.limits: Only `auto`/`bypassPermissions` values are restricted from project/local files; other permission-mode values can be set from any file.

facts.behavior: Managed settings example: `"disableBypassPermissionsMode": "disable"` — the docs describe a policy file with this key as one that "turns off bypass mode." Referenced in the settings-reference summary as: "Prevent anyone from entering bypassPermissions mode."
facts.limits: A "Lock" kind of key under managedSourcesBehavior=merge (strictest value across sources applies).
