facts.behavior: "Subagent files use YAML frontmatter for configuration, followed by the system prompt in Markdown." The frontmatter defines metadata/config; the body becomes the system prompt.
facts.limits: "Subagents receive only this system prompt plus basic environment details like the working directory, not the Claude Code system prompt."

facts.behavior: "Only name and description are required." Multi-word field names use camelCase and must match exactly; "Claude Code ignores unrecognized fields without reporting an error."
facts.limits: name can't contain ':' or start with '-'; description over 15,000 tokens combined across all subagents triggers a startup warning, not a block.

facts.behavior: Controls which built-in/MCP tools a subagent can access. "Inherits every tool available to subagents if omitted."
facts.limits: If nothing in the list resolves to a tool, Claude Code "usually refuses to launch the subagent and the Agent tool returns an error naming the unresolved entries" (before v2.1.208 it launched with zero tools and could return a confusing empty result).

facts.behavior: Accepts an alias (sonnet/opus/haiku/fable), full model ID, or 'inherit'. "Defaults to model order when omitted."
facts.limits: n/a

facts.behavior: "When Claude invokes a subagent, it resolves the model in this order: 1. Per-invocation model parameter (if Claude passes one) 2. Subagent definition's model frontmatter field (where inherit = main conversation's model) 3. CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL environment variable (when set) 4. Main conversation's model." This same default also governs agent team teammates and workflow agents "that aren't assigned a model another way."
facts.limits: Applies only when a per-invocation/definition/env value doesn't otherwise assign a model.

facts.feature: Family alias resolution for subagent models
facts.behavior: "In two cases, a family alias such as opus resolves to the main conversation's model instead of the version the alias points to": when the main conversation's model belongs to that family, or (opus alias only) on a non-Anthropic-API provider with an unresolvable model family, unless ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL is set.
facts.limits: CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL's own value, if an alias, "always resolves to the version the alias points to," even naming the main conversation's family.

facts.feature: Force every subagent onto one model
facts.behavior: Setting CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL plus CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE=1 makes subagents "run on the model in CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL"; FORCE alone makes subagents run on the main conversation's model.
facts.limits: While set, Claude Code ignores every subagent's model field (including built-in Explore/Plan) and Claude can't pass a per-invocation model; forks and skills with model:inherit still run on the main conversation's model.

facts.behavior: "As of v2.1.198, subagents inherit the main conversation's extended thinking configuration: if thinking is on in your session, it's on for the subagent, and if it's off, it stays off. There is no per-subagent thinking setting."
facts.limits: No override exists at the subagent level.

facts.behavior: "Effort level when active: low, medium, high, xhigh, max. Overrides session effort level" for that subagent only.
facts.limits: "Available levels depend on the model"; when omitted, the subagent inherits the session's effort level.

facts.behavior: Model "inherits from the main conversation, capped at Opus on the Claude API" (v2.1.198+); read-only tools (Write/Edit denied).
facts.limits: Never runs on a more expensive model than the main conversation unless CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL is set; overridable by defining a user/project subagent literally named 'Explore'.

facts.behavior: Model "inherits from the main conversation"; read-only tools; used for codebase research inside plan mode.
facts.limits: n/a

facts.behavior: Model "uses CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL if set, otherwise main conversation's model"; has every tool available to subagents.
facts.limits: n/a

facts.feature: availableModels allowlist applied to subagent model resolution
facts.behavior: "Claude Code checks per-invocation parameter, frontmatter, and environment variable values against availableModels allowlist: Blocked family alias (e.g., opus): runs on newest version of that family the allowlist permits. Blocked other value: runs on inherited model instead (or tries CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL first if set)."
facts.limits: Before v2.1.251, CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL came first and overrode the per-invocation parameter and frontmatter.

facts.behavior: Default 3 layers below the main conversation. "At depth limit, Claude Code withholds the Agent tool from subagents (except forks)"; a subagent at the limit does delegated work itself and returns one summary; a fork at the limit keeps Agent in its tool list but the tool errors instead of spawning.
facts.limits: Configurable via CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH (set to 1 to disable nesting entirely); built-in Explore, Plan, and general-purpose can't spawn subagents by default.

facts.behavior: Default 20 concurrent subagents. "When 20 running, spawning another with Agent tool fails: 'Concurrent subagent limit reached'. Error tells Claude not to retry. Spawning succeeds again when running count drops below 20."
facts.limits: Configurable via CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS. "Sessions with ultracode active are exempt; limit not enforced." Workflow agents and agent-team teammates don't count toward it; in-session forks (/subtask) do count and are never blocked by it; requires v2.1.217+.

facts.behavior: Block specific built-ins via permissions.deny (e.g. Agent(Explore), Agent(Plan)) or --disallowedTools; CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPLORE_PLAN_AGENTS=1 disables Explore+Plan only (Claude reads/explores directly instead, v2.1.198+); CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_DISABLE_BUILTIN_AGENTS=1 removes all built-ins in non-interactive mode/SDK (required there); denying the Agent tool itself prevents all delegation.
facts.limits: n/a

facts.behavior: "Maximum agentic turns before stopping. When reached, output marked as partial and Claude can resume."
facts.limits: n/a

facts.behavior: Scopes: user (~/.claude/agent-memory/<name>/), project (.claude/agent-memory/<name>/), local (.claude/agent-memory-local/<name>/). "System prompt includes instructions for reading/writing to memory directory" plus the first 200 lines or 25KB of MEMORY.md; Read/Write/Edit tools are auto-enabled.
facts.limits: "if turned off with autoMemoryEnabled: false or CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY, the memory field has no effect."

facts.behavior: "Set to true to launch without user, project, and local CLAUDE.md files (managed policy files still load). Use for subagents taking everything from delegation prompt."
facts.limits: Requires Claude Code v2.1.271+.

facts.behavior: "Set to worktree to run in temporary git worktree with isolated copy of repository."
facts.limits: n/a

facts.behavior: "Skills to preload into subagent context. Full skill content injected, not only description." Subagent can still discover/invoke other skills via the Skill tool at runtime.
facts.limits: Can't preload a skill with disable-model-invocation: true or the bundled /verify skill; a missing/disabled listed skill "is skipped with warning to debug log."

facts.feature: Agent(agent_type) restriction syntax in tools field
facts.behavior: tools: Agent(worker, researcher) restricts which subagent types this subagent may spawn to only those named. Without an Agent specifier, spawning is unrestricted; without Agent in the tools list at all, the subagent can't spawn any subagents.
facts.limits: n/a

facts.feature: Built-in tool filters applied to subagents
facts.behavior: A first filter removes Agent (at depth limit), AskUserQuestion, EndConversation, EnterPlanMode, ExitPlanMode (unless permissionMode: plan), ScheduleWakeup, WaitForMcpServers, and Workflow from every non-fork subagent; a second filter (background subagents only) restricts to a smaller built-in tool set plus all MCP tools. "Forks skip both filters and receive the main conversation's exact tool pool."
facts.limits: n/a

facts.behavior: "When omitted: subagent inherits main conversation's permission mode." If the main conversation is in bypassPermissions/acceptEdits/auto, the subagent is forced into that same mode regardless of its own setting; if the main conversation is in default/dontAsk/plan, the subagent's own permissionMode applies, except bypassPermissions (the subagent keeps the main conversation's mode instead).
facts.limits: Ignored for plugin subagents.

facts.behavior: Three escalating patterns: natural-language mention (Claude decides whether to delegate), @-mention ("guarantees subagent runs"), and a session-wide agent via --agent flag or the "agent" settings.json key, whose system prompt "replaces the default Claude Code system prompt entirely."
facts.limits: n/a

facts.behavior: Claude automatically delegates based on task description, the subagent's description field, and current context. "To encourage proactive delegation: Include phrases like 'use proactively' in subagent's description field."
facts.limits: Purely advisory phrasing; not a guarantee of delegation.

facts.behavior: Pass JSON defining subagents at launch, supporting prompt plus frontmatter fields description, tools, disallowedTools, model, permissionMode, mcpServers, hooks, maxTurns, skills, initialPrompt, memory, effort, background, omitClaudeMd, isolation.
facts.limits: color and experimental fields are ignored; non-interactive mode (v2.1.281+) can pass a file path instead of JSON, interactive sessions refuse a file path.

facts.behavior: Claude Code scans each subagent's final report before Claude reads it: it inserts a backslash into text imitating harness output (e.g. <\system-reminder> tags, 'Human:'/'Assistant:' lines) and prepends a marker line "[harness: subagent output matched instruction-shaped pattern(s):" when the report imitates tags or mentions permission settings like bypassPermissions.
facts.limits: "Doesn't judge maliciousness. Doesn't change what instruction can do (still goes through permission checks/sandboxing). Not substitute for restricting what subagent can reach." Requires v2.1.210+.

facts.behavior: Rules determine foreground vs background (e.g. in-process teammate spawn -> foreground; CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1 -> foreground; default interactive fork mode -> background; Claude needing the result first -> foreground unless background:true). Background subagents get a reduced built-in tool set (all MCP tools still available); their permission prompts surface in the main session naming the subagent.
facts.limits: n/a

facts.behavior: "An Agent tool call omitting subagent_type fails when session has no general-purpose subagent to fall back on."
facts.limits: n/a

facts.behavior: "Agent teams are experimental and disabled by default. Enable them by setting CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1 in your settings.json or environment. Without that variable, no team is set up at session start, no team directories are written, and Claude does not spawn or propose teammates."
facts.limits: Spawning teammates also requires an interactive session; in non-interactive mode (-p, including Agent SDK) Claude never spawns teammates even with the flag on.

facts.behavior: Subagents: own context window, results return to caller, main agent manages all work, lower token cost. Agent teams: own fully independent context window, teammates message each other directly, self-coordination plus a shared task list, higher token cost (each teammate is a separate Claude instance).
facts.limits: n/a

facts.feature: Implicit teammate spawning when agent teams are enabled
facts.behavior: "Claude launches a teammate when it calls the Agent tool with a name while agent teams are enabled, unless the call is a fork or passes isolation on the call itself... Claude also names ordinary subagents on its own so it can message them later. Those calls follow the same rule, so teams can form even when you didn't ask for one."
facts.limits: "Claude Code doesn't ask you to confirm the launch." Turn off by setting CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS to 0.

facts.feature: Agent team teammate model resolution order
facts.behavior: "Claude Code picks each teammate's model from the first of these that applies: 1. The model your spawn prompt names for that teammate. 2. For a teammate spawned from a subagent definition, the definition's model, where inherit selects the lead's model. 3. CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL, when it's set to anything other than inherit. 4. The lead's current model."
facts.limits: If CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE=1, sources 1-2 don't apply (requires v2.1.257+); before v2.1.251, CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL came first; the teammateDefaultModel setting was removed in v2.1.234 and is ignored.

facts.feature: availableModels allowlist applied to teammate model
facts.behavior: When the allowlist blocks a value: a family alias (e.g. opus) on the Anthropic API/Claude Platform on AWS runs on the newest permitted version of that family; any other blocked value (including an alias on a provider without substitution, or a family with no permitted version) falls back to the lead's model, trying CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL first if set.
facts.limits: n/a

facts.behavior: "Teammates inherit the lead's effort level." /effort still applies to a viewed teammate's later turns because teammates follow the lead's effort level; a teammate's model and fast mode are fixed at spawn, so /model and /fast only change the lead's settings.
facts.limits: In split-pane mode this applies from v2.1.186; earlier versions did not pass the lead's session effort to split-pane teammates.

facts.feature: Teammate plan mode and plan approval
facts.behavior: A teammate spawned while the lead is in plan mode works read-only until its plan is ready, then sends a plan approval request; "Claude Code approves the plan in the lead's session as soon as the request arrives, without the lead reviewing it." The teammate's subsequent edits/commands still go through ordinary permission prompts.
facts.limits: n/a

facts.feature: Shared task list and task claiming
facts.behavior: Tasks have three states (pending, in progress, completed); a pending task with unresolved dependencies "cannot be claimed until those dependencies are completed." The lead can assign explicitly or teammates self-claim. "Task claiming uses file locking to prevent race conditions when multiple teammates try to claim the same task simultaneously."
facts.limits: Agents without the Task tools coordinate through messages instead of the shared task list.

facts.behavior: "TeammateIdle: runs when a teammate is about to go idle. Exit with code 2 to send feedback and keep the teammate working. TaskCreated: runs when a task is being created. Exit with code 2 to prevent creation and send feedback. TaskCompleted: runs when a task is being marked complete. Exit with code 2 to prevent completion and send feedback."
facts.limits: n/a

facts.feature: Team config and task list storage
facts.behavior: Team config lives at ~/.claude/teams/{team-name}/config.json and the task list at ~/.claude/tasks/{team-name}/, named 'session-' plus the first 8 characters of the session ID. The team config directory is removed when the session ends; the task list directory persists locally (never uploaded) so resumed sessions keep their tasks, per cleanupPeriodDays retention.
facts.limits: "There is no project-level equivalent of the team config. A file like .claude/teams/teams.json in your project directory is not recognized as configuration; Claude treats it as an ordinary file." "The team config holds runtime state such as session IDs and tmux pane IDs, so don't edit it by hand or pre-author it: your changes are overwritten on the next state update."

facts.behavior: Each agent's mailbox is a JSON file at ~/.claude/teams/{team-name}/inboxes/{agent-name}.json. "Claude Code validates every entry when it reads a mailbox file. Entries that don't match the message format are reported as errors and removed from the file; the valid messages are still delivered." A message is reported sent only when the write to the recipient's mailbox file succeeds; on a write failure the sender gets an error and nothing is sent.
facts.limits: Before v2.1.207, a single malformed entry caused a repeated error every second and blocked delivery until the file was deleted manually.

facts.feature: Using subagent definitions as teammate roles
facts.behavior: Naming a subagent type when spawning a teammate applies: tools (limited to the definition's list, with SendMessage and, if present, Task tools added for an in-process teammate); model (the definition's model is used when the spawn prompt doesn't name one); body (appended as additional instructions for in-process teammates, used in place of the default prompt for split-pane); mcpServers (applied only for split-pane teammates).
facts.limits: "Claude Code doesn't apply the definition's skills to a teammate in either display mode. The teammate loads skills from your project and user settings."

facts.behavior: "Teammates start with the lead's permission mode, except dontAsk mode, which they don't inherit. If the lead runs with --dangerously-skip-permissions, all teammates do too." You can change an individual teammate's permission mode after spawning.
facts.limits: "you can't set per-teammate permission modes at spawn time." Teammate permission prompts appear in the lead session for the person to approve.

facts.behavior: "When one agent sends another a message over SendMessage, Claude Code tells the receiving agent the message came from another Claude session, not from you. A teammate can't approve a permission prompt or supply consent on your behalf, and a teammate that was denied an action can't relay it to another teammate to bypass the check." In auto mode, the classifier "treats an approval claim relayed from another agent as untrusted input rather than confirmation from you" and reviews every inter-agent message before delivery.
facts.limits: A message the classifier blocks never reaches the recipient.

facts.behavior: "When spawned, a teammate loads the same project context as a regular session: CLAUDE.md, MCP servers, and skills... A teammate also receives the spawn prompt from the lead. The lead's conversation history does not carry over."
facts.limits: n/a

facts.behavior: "An in-process teammate's requests fall outside the main conversation's cache TTL bucket, so its cache holds for five minutes by default, including on a Claude subscription. To keep it for an hour, set subagentPromptCacheTtl to 1h."
facts.limits: The API bills 1-hour cache writes at a higher rate.

facts.behavior: "No session resumption with in-process teammates: /resume and /rewind do not restore in-process teammates." "One team per session." "No nested teams: teammates cannot spawn their own teammates. Only the lead can manage the team." "No background subagents from in-process teammates" (Claude Code errors when a teammate spawns a subagent whose definition sets background: true). "Lead is fixed": can't promote a teammate or transfer leadership. "Permissions set at spawn": no per-teammate mode at spawn time. Split-pane mode requires tmux or iTerm2; not supported in VS Code's integrated terminal, Windows Terminal, or Ghostty.
facts.limits: These are stated as current, acknowledged limitations of an experimental feature, not bugs.

facts.behavior: default clears override and reverts to the account's runtime default; best uses Fable where available, otherwise opus; fable is for the hardest/longest tasks; sonnet/opus/haiku are the latest of each tier; sonnet[1m]/opus[1m] add a 1M-token context window; opusplan uses opus in plan mode and switches to sonnet for execution.
facts.limits: n/a

facts.behavior: opus resolves to Opus 5.5 on the Anthropic API, Claude Platform on AWS, Amazon Bedrock, and Google Cloud Agent Platform, but to Opus 4.6 on Microsoft Foundry; sonnet resolves to Sonnet 5 (Anthropic API), Sonnet 4.6 (Claude Platform on AWS), or Sonnet 4.5 (Bedrock/GCP/Microsoft Foundry).
facts.limits: n/a

facts.behavior: "1. During session: /model <alias|name> command 2. At startup: claude --model <alias|name> flag 3. Environment variable: ANTHROPIC_MODEL=<alias|name> 4. Settings file: model field in settings 5. Default for new sessions: ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL=<alias|name>." "A choice you save with /model takes precedence over the variable on later launches too."
facts.limits: n/a

facts.behavior: "Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise, Anthropic API... Claude Platform on AWS, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Agent Platform: defaults to Opus 5.5. Microsoft Foundry: defaults to Sonnet 4.5." "When an admin has set an organization default model, default resolves to that model instead of the account-type default above."
facts.limits: n/a

facts.behavior: Fable 5.1/5, Opus 5.5/5, Sonnet 5, Opus 4.8/4.7 offer low/medium/high/xhigh/max; Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 offer only low/medium/high/max (no xhigh).
facts.limits: n/a

facts.behavior: "1. Explicit choice: CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL env var, --effort flag, or /effort command 2. Settings: saved level per model or effortLevel key 3. Model's default effort: high on most models, medium on Opus 5.5, xhigh on Opus 4.7, Organization-set default for org default model."
facts.limits: n/a

facts.behavior: "Opus 5.5 starts at medium unless one of the sources above sets a level for it, and a top-level effortLevel in your user settings file doesn't count for Opus 5.5."
facts.limits: Applies specifically to Opus 5.5's default-effort resolution, not other models.

facts.behavior: ANTHROPIC_MODEL sets the model for the current session only; ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL sets the default for new sessions (v2.1.236+); ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL/SONNET_MODEL/HAIKU_MODEL/FABLE_MODEL set what each alias resolves to; CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL sets the default model for subagents/teammates/workflow agents; CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL sets effort and "takes precedence over all other sources."
facts.limits: n/a

facts.behavior: Administrators restrict selectable models; entries match a family, a version prefix, or a full model ID. When a blocked model is selected: "/model: rejected with error"; "--model, ANTHROPIC_MODEL, model setting: replaced at startup with warning"; "ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL: ignored."
facts.limits: A version prefix matches later IDs that extend it with another segment (e.g. claude-fable-5 permits both Fable 5 and 5.1).

facts.behavior: "When that model is not in the allowlist, the Default option instead resolves to the first availableModels entry that names an allowed, available model." Extends allowlist enforcement to the Default option itself.
facts.limits: n/a

facts.behavior: deniedModels blocks specific models even when a family alias would otherwise permit them (v2.1.283+); availableModelsMatch: "exact" restricts selection to only the literally listed model IDs. "A blocked model, whether deniedModels names it or an exact list omits it, is treated as a blocked selection everywhere the allowlist applies."
facts.limits: n/a

facts.behavior: "Organization admins on Claude Enterprise plans restrict which models members can run by disabling individual models in the claude.ai admin console... The restriction applies when a member signs in or uses their own API key." Family aliases then resolve to the newest permitted version.
facts.limits: n/a

facts.behavior: "The organization default is a starting point, not a restriction. These selections take precedence over it: the --model flag and ANTHROPIC_MODEL; a model value in managed settings; a model value in your user, project, or local settings."
facts.limits: Advisory default only; not enforced against explicit choices.

facts.behavior: "Levels above the cap aren't offered in the /effort picker, and naming a higher level with --effort or /effort runs at the cap instead." Caps are set per model and per role; when multiple roles grant the same model, the least restrictive cap applies.
facts.limits: n/a

facts.behavior: Fable 5.1/5 and Sonnet 5 have native 1M context on all plans; Opus 4.7+ has native 1M on the Anthropic API; Opus 4.6/Sonnet 4.6 require the [1m] suffix and have usage requirements (Opus 4.6 1M is included with Max/Team/Enterprise; Sonnet 4.6 1M requires usage credits on every plan).
facts.limits: CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT budgets a session at 200K instead.

facts.behavior: Set via /autocompact (accepts 100k-1M tokens, or shorthand). "Claude Code caps the window at the model's context window." Default thresholds are ~967K tokens for Sonnet 5/1M-window Fable models and a 200K boundary for Sonnet 4.6/Opus 4.6 without extended context.
facts.limits: CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW overrides all other settings for a session.

facts.feature: Extended thinking on fixed-budget vs adaptive-reasoning models
facts.behavior: On models with a fixed thinking budget, MAX_THINKING_TOKENS lowers the budget (e.g. MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=8000); "Adaptive-reasoning models ignore nonzero budgets, so use effort levels there instead." "You can't turn off thinking on Opus 5.5 or the Fable models, which always use extended thinking."
facts.limits: CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADAPTIVE_THINKING reverts adaptive models to a fixed thinking budget.

facts.behavior: ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION adds one custom model to the picker without replacing built-ins. "Claude Code skips validation for the model ID set in ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION, so you can use any string your API endpoint accepts."
facts.limits: For multiple custom models in a custom order, the modelPicker setting is used instead.

facts.behavior: The Session block shows token usage; "Claude Code computes the dollar figure locally from token counts at list price, unless a modelPricing table is in effect." Totals reset on /clear (since v2.1.211; earlier versions accumulated for the process lifetime).
facts.limits: "The figure is an estimate, so for authoritative billing see the Usage page in the Claude Console." The cache-statistics line covers the main conversation only, not subagents.

facts.behavior: "By default, Claude Code computes every cost figure it shows developers at list price... To make them match, set the modelPricing managed setting to your rates. The setting changes what Claude Code reports, not what Anthropic charges."
facts.limits: Deployed only via managed settings; "Claude Code ignores the key in user, project, and local settings and in --settings." Requires v2.1.242+.

facts.behavior: On Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise, /usage shows "recent usage attributed to skills, subagents, plugins, and individual MCP servers, each shown as a percentage of the total," plus behavior flags for things like long context or cache misses when they account for 10% or more of recent usage, and Loops rows for the heaviest scheduled tasks.
facts.limits: Figures are approximate, computed from local session history on this machine only; usage from other devices or claude.ai isn't included.

facts.behavior: "Agent teams use approximately 7x more tokens than standard sessions when teammates run in plan mode, because each teammate maintains its own context window and runs as a separate Claude instance." Guidance: use Sonnet for teammates, keep teams small, keep spawn prompts focused, and shut down teammates when their work is done.
facts.limits: This is stated as guidance, not an enforced cap.

facts.feature: Delegating verbose operations to subagents for cost control
facts.behavior: "Delegate these to subagents so the verbose output stays in the subagent's context while only a summary returns to your main conversation. The subagent's own requests still draw on your usage. To spend less on them, choose a smaller model for a subagent or run every subagent on one model."
facts.limits: n/a

facts.feature: Sources of rising usage: subagents, workflows, teammates
facts.behavior: "Subagents and workflows: every subagent, and every agent a dynamic workflow spawns, sends its own requests on top of the main conversation's." "Agent teammates: each active teammate keeps consuming tokens until it exits."
facts.limits: n/a

facts.behavior: "A dynamic workflow is a JavaScript script that orchestrates many subagents at once. Claude writes the script for the task you describe, and a runtime executes it in the background while your session stays responsive." Available on all paid plans, Anthropic API access, Bedrock, Google Cloud Agent Platform, and Microsoft Foundry.
facts.limits: "On Pro, turn them on from the Dynamic workflows row in /config."

facts.behavior: For workflows, "who decides what runs next" is the script (vs Claude turn-by-turn for subagents/skills, or the lead agent for teams); scale is "Dozens to hundreds of agents per run" vs a few delegated tasks per turn for subagents or a handful of long-running peers for teams; interruption is "Resumable in the same session" vs "Restarts the turn" for subagents/skills.
facts.limits: n/a

facts.behavior: Including 'ultracode' (or phrases like 'use a workflow') in a typed prompt makes Claude write and run a workflow script for that single task without changing the session's effort level.
facts.limits: Works only for prompts typed by a human at the interactive prompt, an IDE panel, Remote Control, or an SDK app that stamps origin as human input; does not trigger from -p prompts, unstamped SDK prompts, scheduled task prompts, webhook payloads, or PR comments (changed in v2.1.210; earlier versions triggered from those routes too).

facts.behavior: "Ultracode is a Claude Code setting that combines xhigh reasoning effort with automatic workflow orchestration. With it on, Claude plans a workflow for each substantive task instead of waiting for you to ask." "This applies to every task in the session, so each request uses more tokens and takes longer... a session with ultracode on reaches a session or weekly limit sooner than the same work at high."
facts.limits: Turning it on exempts the session from the Large-workflow warning, the concurrent-subagent limit for Agent-tool spawns, and the auto-mode first-launch approval prompt. No setting turns off ultracode alone short of capping org effort below xhigh.

facts.feature: Workflow launch approval by permission mode
facts.behavior: Auto mode prompts on first launch only, then remembers consent (skipped entirely with ultracode on); manual/accept-edits modes prompt on every run unless 'don't ask again' was chosen for that workflow in that project; bypass-permissions mode never prompts; claude -p and the Agent SDK never show this prompt and instead route the launch through ordinary permission evaluation (deny/ask/dontAsk rules, a Workflow allow rule, the auto-mode classifier, a PreToolUse hook, or a host permission callback).
facts.limits: n/a

facts.behavior: A run's script can be saved to .claude/workflows/ (project, shared via the repo) or ~/.claude/workflows/ (personal, every project) and then runs as /<name>. "If a project workflow and a personal workflow share a name, the project one runs."
facts.limits: Claude Code refuses to write through a symlink at the save location (checking .claude, .claude/workflows, and the target file for the project location; only the target file for the personal location).

facts.behavior: "No mid-run user input" (pauses only for permission prompts and a usage-limit wait); "No direct filesystem or shell access from the workflow itself" (only spawned agents get it); "No module loading: a script that contains import() fails before the run starts"; "Up to 16 concurrent agents by default, fewer when Claude Code has fewer CPUs available"; "Up to 4,096 items in a single parallel() or pipeline() call: the runtime rejects a longer list with an error"; "1,000 agents total per run."
facts.limits: The concurrent-agent cap is configurable via CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_MAX_CONCURRENT_AGENTS (1-256, requires v2.1.269+); the other caps in this row are fixed.

facts.behavior: "When a workflow schedules more than 25 agents, or its projected token total passes 1.5 million, its progress line... shows a Large workflow warning." "The warning is advisory: it doesn't pause or limit the run."
facts.limits: The 25-agent threshold is replaced by a chosen size guideline's agent count; the warning is not shown when ultracode is on.

facts.behavior: "Claude Code picks each workflow agent's model in the same order it uses for subagents. A model the script names for a stage counts as the per-invocation model in that order. When nothing else assigns one, the agent runs on your session's model." When the availableModels allowlist blocks a script-requested model, the agent runs on a substituted model under the same rules as subagents, and the run's progress view names both the requested and substituted models.
facts.limits: n/a

facts.behavior: "A size guideline tells Claude how many agents to aim for when it writes a dynamic workflow. Claude Code sends the guideline to Claude as advice, not a cap, so a prompt that calls for a different scale still overrides it." Values: unrestricted (no guideline), small (<5 agents), medium (<10, the default), large (<50).
facts.limits: Default is medium, or small on a Pro plan with v2.1.271+; requires v2.1.202+ to exist at all; a settings-file value takes precedence over the /config row.

facts.behavior: Per-user: toggle off in /config, set "disableWorkflows": true in ~/.claude/settings.json, or set CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_WORKFLOWS=1 (read at startup). Org-wide: "disableWorkflows": true in managed settings, or the admin-console toggle. When disabled, bundled workflow commands and the /workflow-authoring skill become unavailable, the ultracode keyword no longer triggers a run, and ultracode is removed from the /effort menu.
facts.limits: A run already in progress keeps going even after workflows are disabled.

facts.behavior: On relaunch: a "Completed" agent returns its saved result unless an earlier agent's output changed, in which case it and every agent after it rerun; an agent "Still running when you stopped: starts over"; a "Failed" agent "runs again, and so does every agent that started after it, even ones that completed."
facts.limits: "If agents from the stopped run haven't exited yet, Claude Code refuses the relaunch until they have."

facts.behavior: "When an agent hits your claude.ai usage limit, the run pauses rather than failing that agent: the agents that hit the limit wait for the reset, and no new agents start... Shortly after the limit resets, the waiting agents run again and the run continues on its own." Requires v2.1.271+; earlier versions fail the affected agents.
facts.limits: Only pauses in an interactive session signed in with a claude.ai subscription, with autoContinueAtUsageLimit on, when the limit resets within 24 hours, and when the run hasn't already waited twice (a third hit fails the agent); doesn't pause in -p/SDK/background/Remote Control/agent-team teammate sessions.

facts.behavior: "Claude Code makes Date.now(), Math.random(), and a no-argument new Date() throw inside the script, so that a relaunched run repeats the same agent() calls. Pass a timestamp in through args instead."
facts.limits: n/a

facts.behavior: "Claude Code checks the schema before starting the subagent: when it can prove the schema contradicts itself, the call fails with an error naming the contradiction, and the subagent never starts." "If the subagent's output still fails validation after five attempts, the call fails with an error that includes the last validation failure."
facts.limits: The retry count is configurable via MAX_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_RETRIES.

area: Claude Code native support for: security model, secrets handling, data usage and retention, and security guidance for agents (as of 2026-09-28)

facts.behavior: In Manual mode, Claude Code starts with read-only permissions; when it needs to edit files, run tests, or execute commands, it asks first, and the user chooses to approve once or allow going forward.
facts.limits: Applies to file edits and non-read-only Bash commands; a built-in read-only command set (ls, cat, git status, etc.) runs without asking. Does not apply in auto mode, acceptEdits, bypassPermissions, or dontAsk modes, which each replace the prompt differently.

facts.behavior: In auto mode, a separate classifier model reviews actions instead of the user and blocks the ones it judges unsafe; explicit ask/deny rules still apply and organizations can turn auto mode off.
facts.limits: Which actions are approved outright, sent to the classifier, or still prompt the user is documented separately (permission-modes#how-the-classifier-evaluates-actions); not available on every plan/session.

facts.feature: Tiered permission system by tool type
facts.behavior: Read-only tools (file reads, Grep) need no approval within working directories; Bash commands need approval except a built-in read-only set; file modification always needs approval; WebFetch needs approval except preapproved documentation domains; WebSearch always needs approval.
facts.limits: "Yes, and don't ask again" persists permanently per repository+command for Bash/WebFetch, but only until session end for file modification.

facts.behavior: Rules are evaluated in order: deny, then ask, then allow. The first match in that order determines the outcome; a broad deny blocks even a matching narrower allow, and rule specificity does not change the order.
facts.limits: Applies uniformly across settings scopes; a user-level deny blocks a project-level allow and vice versa is not true (deny always wins).

facts.feature: Permission rules enforced by Claude Code, not the model
facts.behavior: "Permission rules are enforced by Claude Code, not by the model. Instructions in your prompt or CLAUDE.md shape what Claude tries to do, but they don't change what Claude Code allows."
facts.limits: To actually grant/revoke access requires /permissions, permission rules, a permission mode, or a PreToolUse hook — CLAUDE.md text alone is advisory only and not an enforcement boundary.

facts.behavior: A Bash allow/deny/ask rule matches the command text Claude writes after splitting compound commands and stripping known wrappers; it does not match the same program invoked a different way (e.g. Bash(rm *) deny doesn't stop /bin/rm or bash -c 'rm -rf ...').
facts.limits: Rules are not a security boundary around the underlying program. For enforcement independent of command text, sandboxing or a PreToolUse hook is required.

facts.behavior: PreToolUse hooks run before the permission prompt for every tool except EndConversation and can deny a call, force a prompt, or skip the prompt; a hook that exits with code 2 blocks the call before permission rules are evaluated, taking precedence over allow rules.
facts.limits: Hook decisions never bypass existing deny/ask permission rules — those are still evaluated regardless of what a hook returns.

facts.behavior: In Manual mode, Claude Code can only write to the folder it was started in (and subfolders) and asks before reading paths outside that boundary via Read/Grep/Glob; boundary extends via --add-dir, /add-dir, or permissions.additionalDirectories.
facts.limits: permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories can make file tools hard-refuse outside paths in every mode; sandbox denyRead rules narrow the separately-broader read access available to read-only Bash commands.

facts.feature: Read/Edit deny rules for sensitive files
facts.behavior: Adding a Read deny rule (e.g. Read(./.env), Read(./secrets/**)) blocks Claude's file tools from reading that file/directory and also blocks Edit/Write on the same path, including creating a new file there.
facts.limits: Does not cover NotebookEdit (needs a separate Edit deny rule), does not apply to a Bash command that reads files without naming them (e.g. grep -r pattern .) or to arbitrary subprocesses (e.g. a Python script) reading files indirectly — that requires the sandbox for OS-level enforcement.

facts.behavior: Administrators deploy managed settings (MDM file or server-managed settings) that user and project settings cannot override, apart from a few named security-sensitive keys; e.g. disableBypassPermissionsMode, disableAutoMode, allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly.
facts.limits: No other level, including CLI arguments, can override a managed permission rule/deny.

facts.behavior: permissions.allow rules and permissions.additionalDirectories in a project's .claude/settings.json are applied only after the user accepts a trust dialog for that folder, which lists the rules/directories it would grant; deny/ask rules aren't gated since they only restrict.
facts.limits: Shown only in interactive sessions; a `claude -p` run or SDK session never shows it. Starting in the home directory holds trust for the session only (not written to disk).

facts.behavior: Auto-approves file edits and a fixed set of filesystem Bash commands like mkdir, touch, rm, mv, cp, and sed for paths in the working directory; other Bash commands and out-of-scope paths still prompt.
facts.limits: Only covers the working directory / additionalDirectories; scoped to a fixed command set, not configurable.

facts.behavior: Skips permission prompts entirely, including for writes to protected paths such as .git and .claude, except for a fixed set of actions no mode auto-approves; cross-session messaging safeguards still apply.
facts.limits: Documented as intended "only in isolated environments like containers or VMs where Claude Code can't cause damage." Can be disabled org-wide via permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode.

facts.behavior: OS-level filesystem and network isolation for Bash, PowerShell, and Monitor commands (and child processes), defining which files and network domains commands can touch, enforced by the operating system rather than by Claude Code's decision-making.
facts.limits: Runs on macOS (Seatbelt), Linux and WSL2 (bubblewrap); native Windows is not supported. Only covers Bash/PowerShell/Monitor — not Read/Edit/Write tools or computer use.

facts.behavior: Default write access: current working directory + added directories (--add-dir/permissions.additionalDirectories) + per-user temp directory. Default read access: the entire computer except explicitly denied directories — this still allows reading credential files like ~/.aws/credentials and ~/.ssh/ by default.
facts.limits: Reading credentials requires an explicit sandbox.credentials or denyRead rule to block; the default alone does not protect secrets. Can be turned off entirely (sandbox.filesystem.disabled) while keeping network isolation, only from user/managed/--settings sources, not project settings.

facts.behavior: Within directories a sandboxed command can otherwise write to, the sandbox still denies writes to Claude Code's own config/code paths (.claude settings, skills/agents/commands/hooks dirs, .mcp.json, shell startup files, .git/hooks and config, ~/.claude and .credentials.json, etc.) so a running command can't grant itself permissions.
facts.limits: "There is no way to exempt one of these paths": an allowWrite or Edit allow rule covering the path doesn't lift the protection; only filesystem.disabled turns off the whole filesystem layer (widening everything, not just this).

facts.behavior: Network access goes through a proxy outside the sandbox; Claude Code pre-allows no domains by default, and the first time a command needs a new domain it prompts for approval (or, in auto mode, the command names required hosts for classifier review).
facts.limits: strictAllowlist (user/managed/CLI settings only, not project) denies instead of prompting; allowManagedDomainsOnly (managed settings) enforces an org-locked allowlist automatically. By default the proxy does not terminate/inspect TLS, so encrypted content is not examined and domain fronting to reach non-allowed hosts is a documented risk.

facts.behavior: sandbox.credentials.files/envVars with mode "deny" denies file-path reads inside the sandbox (like filesystem.denyRead) and unsets named environment variables before each sandboxed command runs.
facts.limits: No built-in credential deny list exists — only files/variables explicitly listed are restricted. File protection is part of the filesystem layer, so it does not apply if filesystem isolation is disabled; env-var protection still applies regardless.

facts.behavior: mode "mask" shows sandboxed commands a placeholder sentinel value instead of the real credential (env var or file); the sandbox proxy substitutes the real value on outbound requests to allowed hosts (injectHosts), so tools keep authenticating without the command or its logs ever holding the real secret.
facts.limits: Requires network.tlsTerminate for the proxy to see and substitute request contents; honored only from user settings, managed settings, or --settings CLI flag (ignored in repo-level .claude/settings.json). On macOS, file masking falls back to full deny (file unreadable) rather than a sentinel copy.

facts.behavior: When a command can't run inside the sandbox, Claude Code reports the sandbox violation and Claude may retry the command with dangerouslyDisableSandbox, which runs it outside the sandbox through the regular (non-sandbox) permission flow.
facts.limits: Can be fully disabled with sandbox.allowUnsandboxedCommands:false ("strict sandbox mode"), after which Claude Code ignores the parameter and every Claude-run command must be sandboxed unless explicitly excluded.

facts.behavior: "The operating system enforces the sandbox boundary on the running process, so it holds regardless of what the model chose to run and even if an allowed command does more than its name suggests" — distinct from permission rules, which are evaluated before the command runs based on the command string.
facts.limits: Sandbox restrictions still apply even if a prompt injection bypasses Claude's decision-making, per the docs' defense-in-depth framing; permission rules alone do not provide this guarantee.

facts.behavior: Claude Code "detects potentially harmful instructions by analyzing the full request" as one of several core protections against prompt injection.
facts.limits: No detail given on detection accuracy or what happens on a positive detection beyond routing into the normal permission flow; documented as one layer among several, explicitly not complete: "no system is completely immune to all attacks."

facts.behavior: "Prevents command injection by processing user inputs" as a core protection against prompt injection attacks.
facts.limits: No further mechanism detail documented on this page.

facts.behavior: Commands that fetch content from the web such as curl and wget are not auto-approved by default; in Manual mode they prompt like any other non-read-only Bash command. To block them outright, add them to permissions.deny.
facts.limits: A deny rule matches the command as written (text-based), so it isn't reliable network enforcement on its own; for enforcement independent of command text, sandbox network isolation is needed.

facts.behavior: "Web fetch uses a separate context window to avoid injecting potentially malicious prompts" into the main conversation.
facts.limits: Applies specifically to the WebFetch tool.

facts.feature: Trust verification for new codebases/MCP servers
facts.behavior: First-time codebase runs and new MCP servers require trust verification (the workspace trust dialog).
facts.limits: Disabled when running non-interactively with -p. Starting Claude Code directly in the home directory holds trust for the current session only, not written to disk, so the prompt reappears every launch.

facts.behavior: In Manual mode, suspicious bash commands require manual approval even if previously allowlisted.
facts.limits: Manual-mode specific behavior; no detail on the detection heuristic.

facts.behavior: In Manual mode, unmatched commands require approval by default (rather than silently running).
facts.limits: Manual-mode specific.

facts.feature: Natural language descriptions of bash commands
facts.behavior: "Complex bash commands include explanations for user understanding" to aid the approval decision.
facts.limits: Advisory aid to the human reviewer, not an enforcement mechanism itself.

facts.behavior: Anthropic recommends against enabling WebDAV or allowing Claude Code to access paths such as \\* that may contain WebDAV subdirectories on Windows, because it "may allow Claude Code to trigger network requests to remote hosts, bypassing the permission system."
facts.limits: Windows-specific; documented as a warning/recommendation, not a built-in block.

facts.behavior: Documented advisory practices: review suggested commands before approval, avoid piping untrusted content directly to Claude, verify proposed changes to critical files, use VMs when interacting with external web services, report suspicious behavior with /feedback.
facts.limits: Purely advisory guidance in docs; not enforced by the product.

facts.behavior: API keys/tokens: macOS stores credentials in the encrypted macOS Keychain (falling back to ~/.claude/.credentials.json mode 0600 if the Keychain is unwritable, e.g. locked SSH session); Linux stores in ~/.claude/.credentials.json mode 0600; Windows stores in %USERPROFILE%\.claude\.credentials.json, inheriting the user profile directory's access controls.
facts.limits: If CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is set, the credentials file (and the macOS Keychain entry) is keyed to that directory instead, so a session with a different CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR reads a different credential entry.

facts.behavior: Configure the apiKeyHelper setting to run a shell script that returns an API key; Claude Code re-runs it every 5 minutes by default (configurable via CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_HELPER_TTL_MS) and warns if it takes over 10 seconds.
facts.limits: Applies to the CLI and surfaces that wrap it (VS Code extension, Agent SDK, GitHub Actions); Claude Desktop and cloud sessions do not call apiKeyHelper.

facts.behavior: Strips credentials from all subprocesses regardless of sandboxing (broader than sandbox.credentials, which affects sandboxed Bash commands only); also forces every command, including shell-mode (!) commands, to run sandboxed on Linux, and prevents filesystem.disabled from being honored from any settings source.
facts.limits: Environment-variable driven; no scope limit documented beyond "all subprocesses."

facts.behavior: The list of allowed MCP servers is configured in source-controlled Claude Code settings; Anthropic reviews connectors against listing criteria before adding them to the Anthropic Directory, but "does not security-audit or manage any MCP server." Anthropic recommends writing your own MCP servers or using ones from trusted providers.
facts.limits: Directory review criteria apply only to connectors listed in the Anthropic Directory, not arbitrary MCP servers a user configures.

facts.behavior: Each cloud session runs in an isolated, Anthropic-managed VM; network access is limited by default and configurable (disabled or domain-restricted); GitHub credentials are stored encrypted server-side and never enter the session VM (short-lived scoped credential + server-side proxy attaches it); git push is restricted to the current working branch; all operations are audit-logged; session VMs are reclaimed after inactivity; sessions can be deleted anytime.
facts.limits: Applies to Anthropic-hosted cloud sessions specifically. Sessions routed to a self-hosted environment run on customer infrastructure, where isolation/egress/git-credentials are the deployment's own responsibility, not Anthropic's.

facts.behavior: Remote Control connects the web interface to a local Claude Code process; all code execution and file access stays local, session traffic travels over the Anthropic API via TLS, and while connected the session transcript is stored on Anthropic servers to sync the conversation across devices. The connection uses multiple short-lived, narrowly scoped credentials, each limited to a specific purpose and expiring independently.
facts.limits: "No cloud VMs or sandboxing are involved" — distinct from cloud sessions; the transcript storage-for-sync is a documented exception to "stays local."

facts.behavior: Documented recommendations: use managed settings to enforce organizational standards, share approved permission configs via version control, train team members on security best practices, monitor usage via OpenTelemetry metrics, and audit/block settings changes during sessions with ConfigChange hooks.
facts.limits: Mix of advisory guidance (training, sharing configs) and actual enforceable mechanisms (managed settings, ConfigChange hooks).

facts.behavior: Security vulnerabilities in Claude Code itself should not be disclosed publicly; report via the HackerOne program with detailed reproduction steps and allow time before public disclosure.
facts.limits: This is about vulnerabilities in Claude Code the product, not a scanning tool for a user's own code.

facts.behavior: An installable plugin that makes Claude review its own code changes for common vulnerabilities (injection, unsafe deserialization, unsafe DOM APIs, etc.) while it works and fix what it finds in the same session, before the code reaches a pull request. Runs automatically once installed; nothing to invoke.
facts.limits: Not installed by default; requires Python 3.7+ (3.10+ for agentic commit review and third-party providers), a git repository (end-of-turn/commit reviews skip silently outside one), and network/pip access on first run to install the Claude Agent SDK.

facts.behavior: On each file edit, scans new content for known risky patterns (eval(, os.system, dangerouslySetInnerHTML, .innerHTML=, .github/workflows/ edits, etc.) via deterministic string/regex match with no model call; appends a warning to Claude's context for the next step, once per pattern per file per session.
facts.limits: Pattern list cannot be removed, only extended (via security-patterns.yaml, up to 50 custom rules) or the whole layer disabled (ENABLE_PATTERN_RULES=0). Does not block the write.

facts.behavior: After each turn, computes a git diff of everything changed (Bash, edit tools, subagents included) and sends it to a separate Claude review focused on security, running in the background; findings re-prompt Claude to fix them as a follow-up. Covers up to 30 changed files per turn, fires at most three times in a row before yielding to the user.
facts.limits: Requires a git repo and Anthropic authentication (or configured third-party provider); doesn't block/delay the reply. Disable via ENABLE_STOP_REVIEW=0.

facts.behavior: When Claude runs git commit or git push via its Bash tool, a deeper agentic background review reads surrounding code (callers, sanitizers, related files) to reduce false positives before reporting findings, re-prompting Claude only for new findings.
facts.limits: Fires only on commits/pushes Claude runs through its Bash tool, not ones run from the user's own shell or the `!` shell-escape. Capped at 20 reviews per rolling hour. Disable via ENABLE_COMMIT_REVIEW=0.

facts.behavior: The per-edit check is a deterministic string match with no model; the end-of-turn/commit reviews run as a separate Claude call with fresh context and a security-focused prompt. "None of the layers block writes or commits. Findings reach the writing Claude as instructions... the review model can miss issues. Treat the plugin as one layer of defense in depth, not a complete security solution."
facts.limits: Explicitly documented as non-blocking and imperfect (may miss issues); pair with other layers (/security-review, Claude Security plugin, PR-time Code Review, CI scanners) for defense-in-depth.

facts.behavior: A project can add .claude/claude-security-guidance.md (plus user-scope and .local variants) describing a threat model/checklist in plain language, which the model-backed reviews load as additional context; combined cap of 8KB.
facts.limits: "Additive only: a rule that says to ignore a vulnerability class does not suppress those findings"; not a hard guardrail. For hard enforcement, docs recommend pairing with a hook that blocks the edit or a CI check.

facts.behavior: .claude/security-patterns.yaml (or .yml/.json) adds regex/substring rules to the deterministic per-edit check, each with rule_name, reminder (capped 1KB), regex or substrings, optional paths/exclude_paths globs.
facts.limits: Up to 50 custom rules loaded; regexes that look prone to catastrophic backtracking are skipped; YAML requires PyYAML importable or the file is ignored (JSON works without it).

facts.behavior: The per-edit pattern check makes no model call and adds no cost. The end-of-turn and commit reviews each use additional model usage counted toward normal usage, both by default using Claude Opus 4.7 (configurable via SECURITY_REVIEW_MODEL / SG_AGENTIC_MODEL). Available on all plans.
facts.limits: Commit review is agentic and may take several model turns per commit.

facts.behavior: Runs an on-demand, single-pass security review of the changes on the current branch, when the user asks.
facts.limits: One-time pass on the current branch's diff only — not the whole repository, not automatic.

facts.behavior: A deeper multi-agent vulnerability scan of a repository or diff, with independently reviewed findings and patches, for finding issues in code already present rather than just changes Claude is writing.
facts.limits: On-demand, invoked by the user; distinct from the always-on security-guidance plugin and from /security-review's single-branch-diff scope.

facts.behavior: Multi-agent correctness and security review with full codebase context, run on pull requests, available on Team and Enterprise plans.
facts.limits: PR-time only, not in-session; plan-gated (Team/Enterprise).

facts.behavior: Free/Pro/Max users can choose whether their data (including Claude Code usage from these accounts) is used to train future Claude models; Anthropic trains new models on this data when the setting is on.
facts.limits: Consumer plans only; toggle at claude.ai/settings/privacy (or claude.ai/settings/data-privacy-controls).

facts.behavior: "Anthropic does not train generative models using code or prompts sent to Claude Code under commercial terms" (Team, Enterprise, API, 3rd-party platforms, Claude Gov), unless the customer opted in (e.g. Development Partner Program).
facts.limits: Applies to Team/Enterprise/API/3rd-party-platform/Gov usage specifically; opt-in program is Anthropic-first-party-API only, not available on Bedrock or Vertex.

facts.behavior: Sending feedback via /feedback (and /bug, /share, which report through the same path) sends a copy of conversation history including code to Anthropic; the user chooses how much history to include (current session by default, or last 24h/7d of the project) before submitting; transcripts are retained for 5 years; data is TLS-encrypted in transit and stored in Google Cloud Storage (encrypted at rest by default); optionally opens a public GitHub issue.
facts.limits: Opt out with DISABLE_FEEDBACK_COMMAND=1. On third-party providers (Bedrock/Vertex) or with no Anthropic credentials, /feedback instead writes a locally-archived bundle under ~/.claude/feedback-bundles/ (known key/token patterns redacted) that nothing sends off-machine until the user forwards it.

facts.behavior: Claude can draft a feedback report and queue it locally for the user to review; Claude Code sends nothing until the user chooses to send the draft, after which it goes through the same submission path/retention as other /feedback reports.
facts.limits: Drafting alone never transmits data; transmission requires explicit user action.

facts.behavior: The "How is Claude doing this session?" prompt, including selecting "Dismiss", records only the rating — "we do not collect or store any conversation transcripts, inputs, outputs, or other session data as part of the rating prompt itself."
facts.limits: Distinct from thumbs up/down feedback or /feedback reports, which do send data.

facts.behavior: A separate optional follow-up ("Can Anthropic look at your session transcript...") only uploads the transcript, subagent transcripts, and raw session log file on an explicit "Yes" (known API key/token patterns redacted first; source code and other content uploaded as-is); retained up to 6 months. "No" sends nothing; "Don't ask again" stops future prompts. On Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry/gateway sessions, "Yes" writes the same payload to a local archive under ~/.claude/feedback-bundles/ instead of uploading.
facts.limits: Never shown for organizations with zero data retention, product-feedback disabled by org policy, or CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC set. Responses "do not impact your data training preferences and cannot be used to train our AI models." Disable via CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_FEEDBACK_SURVEY=1 (also disabled by DISABLE_TELEMETRY/DO_NOT_TRACK/CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC).

facts.behavior: Consumer: 5-year retention if data-use-for-training is allowed, 30-day retention if not. Commercial (Team/Enterprise/API) standard: 30-day retention. Zero Data Retention (ZDR) available to qualified Enterprise accounts, enabled per-organization by the account team.
facts.limits: ZDR is not included in standard Enterprise and requires separate enablement; not automatic for new orgs under the same account.

facts.behavior: Claude Code clients store session transcripts locally in plaintext under ~/.claude/projects/ for 30 days by default (to enable session resumption), adjustable via cleanupPeriodDays.
facts.limits: Transcripts of sessions started or most recently continued in Claude Desktop or Cowork are exempt from that limit by default.

facts.behavior: Users can delete individual cloud sessions at any time; deleting a session permanently removes the session's event data.
facts.limits: Applies to cloud sessions specifically.

facts.behavior: Anthropic API: infrastructure-level AES-256 disk encryption, with Zero Data Retention available for no server-side persistence. Bedrock: AES-256 with AWS-managed keys (customer-managed via KMS available). Vertex: Google-managed keys (CMEK available). Microsoft Foundry: depends on hosting option (Hosted-on-Azure keeps prompts/completions within Azure; Hosted-on-Anthropic uses Anthropic's AES-256).
facts.limits: Table applies to server-side storage per model provider, not local disk.

facts.behavior: Data sent to interact with the LLM, including all user prompts and model outputs, is encrypted in transit via TLS 1.2+; Claude Code is compatible with most popular VPNs and LLM proxies.
facts.limits: Covers the network hop between the client and the model provider.

facts.behavior: The repository is cloned into an isolated session VM; Anthropic stores the session transcript for resumption, subject to standard retention/usage policy; GitHub credentials are stored encrypted server-side and never enter the VM, with traffic going through an Anthropic proxy; all outbound traffic goes through a security proxy for audit logging/abuse prevention.
facts.limits: For self-hosted environments, infrastructure the org controls; see self-hosted-environments docs for what stays on customer infra vs. what still reaches Anthropic.

facts.behavior: Latency, reliability, and usage-pattern metrics are sent to Anthropic and third-party logging infrastructure over TLS. "Metrics never include your code, prompts, or file paths."
facts.limits: Opt out via DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1. Default on for direct Anthropic API; default off for Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry unless their USE_* env var is set to 1 (or CLAUDE_CODE_PROVIDER_MANAGED_BY_HOST changes the default to on).

facts.behavior: Error messages and stack traces from Claude Code's own internals are sent to a third-party error-tracking service over TLS; "Claude Code redacts known patterns of secrets, file paths, email addresses, and other personal information before anything leaves your machine."
facts.limits: On only when: signed in with Pro/Max subscription, v2.1.198+, connecting directly to the Claude API, and the org has no ZDR or HIPAA agreement. Opt out via DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING=1.

facts.behavior: Before fetching a URL, WebFetch sends the requested hostname (only the hostname, not the full URL/path/contents) to api.anthropic.com to check it against an Anthropic-maintained safety blocklist; a passing hostname is cached 5 minutes, a blocked/failed one is re-checked next request.
facts.limits: Runs regardless of model provider and is unaffected by CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC. Disabling it (skipWebFetchPreflight: true in settings) means WebFetch attempts any URL without consulting the blocklist — combine with WebFetch permission rules to restrict domains if disabled.

facts.behavior: A single environment variable that disables all non-essential Anthropic-bound traffic at once: telemetry, error reporting, and (with DISABLE_TELEMETRY) feature-flag evaluation, plus it suppresses the session-quality-survey transcript follow-up.
facts.limits: Does not affect the WebFetch domain safety check or the official plugin marketplace auto-install — each has its own separate opt-out (skipWebFetchPreflight, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_OFFICIAL_MARKETPLACE_AUTOINSTALL).

facts.behavior: When enabled (qualified Claude for Enterprise orgs only, enabled per-org by Anthropic after eligibility confirmation), "prompts and model responses generated during Claude Code sessions are processed in real time and not stored by Anthropic after the response is returned, except where needed to comply with law or combat misuse." Covers model inference calls through Claude Code on Claude for Enterprise, for every model available to the org.
facts.limits: Not included in standard Enterprise plan; applies only to Anthropic's direct platform (not Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry, which follow those platforms' own policies); each new org under the same account needs separate enablement. Data may still be retained up to 2 years for Usage Policy violations.

facts.behavior: Even with ZDR on: Chat on claude.ai (via Enterprise web) is not covered; Cowork sessions are not covered; Claude Code Analytics does not store prompts/responses but does collect productivity metadata (account emails, usage stats); user/seat management data follows standard retention; third-party integrations/MCP servers' data handling is outside ZDR entirely.
facts.limits: These follow "standard data retention policies" instead — listed explicitly as exceptions to the ZDR guarantee.

facts.behavior: When ZDR is enabled, features requiring stored prompts/completions are automatically disabled at the backend: Cloud sessions (including from Desktop), Claude Tag, Artifacts, feedback submission (/feedback, /bug, /share), and Remote Control. "These features are blocked in the backend regardless of client-side display" — attempting to use one returns a policy error.
facts.limits: Documented as possibly growing: "Future features may also be disabled if they require storing prompts or completions."

facts.feature: Data access scope for cloud sessions
facts.behavior: "For remote Claude Code, Claude accesses the repository where you initiate your Claude Code session. Claude does not access repositories that you have connected but have not started a session in."
facts.limits: Applies to cloud/remote sessions; local sessions are scoped by the working directory boundary instead.

facts.behavior: An organization admin can explicitly opt in to provide materials for Anthropic to train on, via the Development Partner Program; only then are those materials used for model training under commercial terms.
facts.limits: Available only for Anthropic first-party API; not available for Bedrock or Vertex users.

area: Claude Code native features: hooks (events, matchers, blocking semantics, JSON output), permissions, settings layering, managed policy settings — as of 2026-09-28

facts.behavior: Hooks are user-defined shell commands, HTTP endpoints, MCP tool calls, LLM prompts, or subagents that execute automatically at specific points in Claude Code's lifecycle. Events fall into three cadences: per session (SessionStart, SessionEnd), per turn (UserPromptSubmit, Stop, StopFailure), and on every tool call (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, except EndConversation calls). Full event list: SessionStart, Setup, UserPromptSubmit, UserPromptExpansion, PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, PermissionDenied, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PostToolBatch, Notification, MessageDisplay, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, TaskCreated, TaskCompleted, Stop, StopFailure, TeammateIdle, InstructionsLoaded, ConfigChange, CwdChanged, DirectoryAdded, FileChanged, WorktreeCreate, WorktreeRemove, PreCompact, PostCompact, PreModelSwitch, PostModelSwitch, Elicitation, ElicitationResult, SessionEnd.
facts.limits: Not every event supports blocking or matchers; e.g. CwdChanged has no matcher support and always fires.

facts.behavior: The matcher field filters when hooks fire, evaluated as: exact match (or | / , separated list) for names of letters/digits/_/-/spaces, unanchored JS regex if it contains any other character, or match-all for '*', '' or omitted. Each event type matches on a different field (e.g. tool name for PreToolUse/PostToolUse, session-start reason for SessionStart).
facts.limits: FileChanged and StopFailure use a narrower exact-match set (letters, digits, _, | only); adding a matcher to an event without matcher support is silently ignored.

facts.behavior: Five hook handler types: command (runs a shell command, JSON on stdin, exit codes/stdout communicate results), http (POST JSON to a URL, same JSON response format), mcp_tool (calls a tool on a configured MCP server), prompt (single-turn Claude model evaluation returning JSON 'ok'/'reason'), and agent (spawns a subagent with tool access, experimental).
facts.limits: Agent hooks are explicitly experimental and 'may change'; production workflows are told to prefer command hooks.

facts.behavior: Exit 2 means a blocking error. On events that can block, exit 2 blocks whether or not JSON is printed: even a JSON permissionDecision of 'allow' can't override it. What the block does varies by event (e.g. PreToolUse blocks the tool call, UserPromptSubmit rejects the prompt).
facts.limits: Not all events can block on exit 2 (e.g. PermissionRequest ignores exit code 2 entirely; use the decision object instead). WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove use their own any-nonzero-exit rule instead of the exit-2 rule.

facts.feature: Hook exit code 0 / other codes and JSON output
facts.behavior: Exit 0 means success/no objection; for a PreToolUse hook this does NOT approve the call — the normal permission flow still applies. For structured control, a hook exits 0 and prints a JSON object to stdout (e.g. hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision: allow/deny/ask/defer). Any exit code other than 2: if stdout is valid JSON that passes schema validation, Claude Code ignores the exit code and the JSON alone decides the outcome.
facts.limits: A parsed object failing schema validation, or unparseable JSON-looking stdout, is a non-blocking error (action proceeds) on any exit code other than 2. Exit code 1 alone (no valid JSON) does NOT block, contrary to Unix convention.

facts.behavior: On PreToolUse, Claude Code handles permissionDecision as: 'allow' skips the interactive prompt (deny/ask rules and requiresUserInteraction/organization-ask connector tools still apply); 'deny' cancels the call and sends the reason to Claude; 'ask' shows the normal prompt; 'defer' (non-interactive -p mode only) preserves the call for an Agent SDK wrapper to resume.
facts.limits: 'allow' cannot bypass deny rules, enterprise managed deny lists, or prompts required for tools marked requiresUserInteraction.

facts.feature: Combining results from multiple matching hooks
facts.behavior: When multiple hooks match the same event, every hook's command runs to completion before Claude Code merges the results; one hook returning deny doesn't stop sibling hooks from executing. For PreToolUse permission decisions, the most restrictive answer applies, in the order deny, defer, ask, allow. Text from additionalContext is kept from every hook.
facts.limits: Don't rely on one hook's deny to suppress side effects in another hook — side effects (e.g. a log write) from a sibling hook still occur.

facts.feature: Hooks and permission modes (hooks can't be bypassed by mode)
facts.behavior: PreToolUse hooks fire before any permission-mode check, in every permission mode including dontAsk. A hook that returns permissionDecision: deny blocks the tool even in bypassPermissions mode or with --dangerously-skip-permissions. This lets you enforce policy that users can't bypass by changing their permission mode.
facts.limits: The reverse is not true: a hook returning 'allow' doesn't bypass deny rules from settings, and can't suppress prompts for MCP tools marked requiresUserInteraction or org-ask connector tools. Hooks can tighten but not loosen restrictions.

facts.behavior: Where a hook is defined determines its scope: ~/.claude/settings.json (all your projects, not shareable), .claude/settings.json (single project, shareable/committable), .claude/settings.local.json (single project, not shareable/gitignored), managed policy settings (organization-wide, admin-controlled), plugin hooks/hooks.json (while plugin enabled), skill frontmatter (rest of session once invoked), subagent frontmatter (while that subagent runs).
facts.limits: Hook entries merge across settings levels rather than replacing each other; disableAllHooks set outside managed settings can't disable managed hooks.

facts.behavior: Set 'disableAllHooks': true in a settings file to temporarily disable all hooks from that scope without removing them; Claude Code reads the value left after settings precedence applies, so a project's settings file can override a user file's value.
facts.limits: Hooks configured in managed settings still run unless disableAllHooks is also set at the managed settings level — only managed-level disableAllHooks can disable managed hooks. There is no way to disable an individual hook while keeping it in the configuration.

facts.behavior: Administrators can use allowManagedHooksOnly to restrict which hooks run: user, project, local, and plugin hooks are blocked (hooks from plugins force-enabled in managed settings enabledPlugins are exempt). It also narrows statusLine/fileSuggestion/subagentStatusLine to managed settings and disables command-sourced plugins unless disableCommandPluginSources is explicitly false.
facts.limits: Managed-only setting: can only be set from a managed source, not from user/project/local settings files.

facts.behavior: allowedHttpHookUrls: when defined at any settings level, Claude Code runs an HTTP hook handler only if its URL matches the merged allowlist. httpHookAllowedEnvVars: when defined, Claude Code interpolates only the listed environment variables into hook headers. Both apply to hooks from every source, including managed policy settings.
facts.limits: These allowlists merge across settings files (not restricted to managed source alone), unlike many other managed-only locks.

facts.behavior: Claude Code overrides a Stop hook after it blocks eight times in a row without progress, ending the turn with a warning. Hook scripts should check the stop_hook_active field and exit early if true. If a hook legitimately needs more iterations, raise the cap with CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP.
facts.limits: The 8-block cap is the default; configurable only via the CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP environment variable, not a settings key.

facts.behavior: Default timeouts: 600s for command/http/mcp_tool hooks (30s for UserPromptSubmit/PreModelSwitch/PostModelSwitch, 10s for MessageDisplay), 30s for prompt hooks, 60s for agent hooks. SessionEnd hooks of any type share a 1.5s budget (raised to match a longer per-hook timeout, up to 60s). A command hook run with async:true is not subject to Claude Code's timeout enforcement.
facts.limits: On PreToolUse, a timed-out command/http/mcp_tool hook does NOT block the tool call — it continues through normal permission flow ("don't count on a stalled hook to act as a gate"); only an Agent SDK callback hook that times out blocks the call.

facts.behavior: The if field on an individual hook handler uses permission rule syntax (e.g. "Bash(git *)", "Edit(*.ts)") to filter by tool name and arguments together, beyond what matcher (tool-name-only) can do. Only evaluated on tool events: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PermissionRequest, PermissionDenied.
facts.limits: The if filter is best-effort for Bash: when Claude Code can't determine which commands a Bash input runs, it runs the hook regardless of the pattern — 'use the permission system rather than a hook to enforce a hard allow or deny.' Adding if to a non-tool event prevents the hook from running at all.

facts.behavior: For decisions requiring judgment, type:'prompt' hooks send the hook's input data to a Claude model (Haiku by default) for single-turn evaluation; the model returns JSON {"ok": true} or {"ok": false, "reason": ...}. On PreToolUse a deny by default ends the turn (reason shown as a warning) unless continueOnBlock:true feeds the reason back to Claude to continue.
facts.limits: Default 30s timeout; can specify a different model with the model field.

facts.behavior: Agent hooks spawn a subagent that can read files, search code, and use other tools to verify conditions before returning an 'ok'/'reason' decision, with up to 50 tool-use turns and a 60s default timeout.
facts.limits: Explicitly labeled experimental; behavior/configuration may change; no continueOnBlock field (behaves as if it were always set).

facts.behavior: Read-only tools (file reads, Grep) need no approval within working/additional directories. Bash commands need approval except a built-in read-only set. File modification (Edit/write) always needs approval, lasting only until session end even with 'don't ask again'. WebFetch needs approval except preapproved documentation domains, approved permanently per repo+domain. WebSearch needs approval, approved permanently per repository.
facts.limits: 'Yes, and don't ask again' persistence differs by tool type — file-modification approvals are session-only and never written to a settings file.

facts.behavior: Rules are evaluated in order: deny, then ask, then allow. The first match in that order determines the outcome, and rule specificity doesn't change the order. A broad deny rule blocks even a call that also matches a narrower allow rule.
facts.limits: Permission rules are enforced by Claude Code, not by the model — CLAUDE.md instructions shape what Claude tries but never change what Claude Code allows.

facts.behavior: A bare tool name like 'Bash' as a deny rule removes the tool from Claude's context entirely, so Claude never sees it/can't call it. A scoped rule like 'Bash(rm *)' leaves the tool available and blocks matching calls when attempted.
facts.limits: Bare-name removal applies to every tool except EndConversation: a deny rule can't remove it while any other tool remains.
